definition_en: a small bag carried in the hand or on the arm, holding personal things
core_image: 一只提在手腕上的方形小包，装着钥匙、钱包和口红
scene: 出门前妈妈站在穿衣镜前，把手机、钥匙一样样放进提包。 She carried a leather handbag to the office party.
sceneCN: 这里 handbag 是「手提包」（第 1 个义项：手提收纳个人物品的袋）；句意是她拎着一只皮质手袋去参加公司聚会。

derivatives.zh: handbag 的基础词，义为「袋子」
美式对应说法，义为「手袋；钱包」

senses.title: A personal carry bag
senses.definition: a small bag holding money, keys, and personal items
senses.definitionCN: 装钱、钥匙与私人物品的小包
senses.example: Her handbag matched her shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手袋和鞋子很配套。
senses.why: The picture is a palm-sized container held in the hand, so the object itself leads.
senses.whyCN: 画面是握在手中的小容器，物件本身即为第一义项。

senses.title: The bag as a fashion item
senses.definition: a handbag chosen for style or brand, not just use
senses.definitionCN: 以款式或品牌为选择标准的手袋
senses.example: Designer handbags cost more than phones.
senses.exampleCN: 名牌手袋比手机还贵。
senses.why: Once an object is carried daily, fashion claims it and the price follows.
senses.whyCN: 日常随身之物被时尚收编，价格也随之攀升。

senses.title: The contents carried
senses.definition: the personal items inside the bag, as in search her handbag
senses.definitionCN: 包内的私人物品，如搜查手袋
senses.example: The guard checked each handbag at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 保安在门口逐一检查手袋。
senses.why: The container stands for what it holds, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 容器代指所装之物，英语常见此类转喻。

senses.title: A prize or status symbol
senses.definition: an expensive bag showing wealth or rank
senses.definitionCN: 展示财富或地位的名贵包
senses.example: In the film the villain judges everyone by their handbag.
senses.exampleCN: 电影里反派以手袋评判他人。
senses.why: Fashion value turns into social signal; the bag speaks before its owner does.
senses.whyCN: 时尚价值转化为社交信号，包先于主人开口说话。

intro.en: Handbag is a young compound, younger than the two words that build it.
intro.cn: handbag 是个年轻的合成词，比构成它的两个词都年轻。

items.en: Old English hand named the grasping limb.
items.cn: 古英语 hand 指抓握之肢。

items.en: Old Norse baggi gave English bag for a sack or pouch.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 baggi 给英语带来 bag，指袋、囊。

items.en: Middle English used bags for travel and money pouches.
items.cn: 中古英语用 bag 指旅行行囊与钱袋。

items.en: In the mid-nineteenth century handbag was coined for a bag carried in the hand.
items.cn: 十九世纪中叶人们造出 handbag 一词，指手提之袋。

items.en: Twentieth-century fashion turned the word into a luxury category.
items.cn: 二十世纪时尚业把该词变成奢侈品类目。

note.en: Words near handbag in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 handbag 形近或义近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 戏谑用法，挥舞手袋（罕用）

entries.definition: a small bell rung by hand
entries.definitionCN: 手铃；同构词但意义无关

entries.definition: a small reference book held in the hand
entries.definitionCN: 手册；同前缀合成词，便于对照

entries.definition: a small bag for money, American sense
entries.definitionCN: （美式）手袋；钱包

entries.definition: a bag carried on the back

entries.definition: a flat case for money and cards
entries.definitionCN: 钱包，仅收纳钱证

normalIntro.cn: 五条 handbag 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: hand + bag literally a bag in the hand
normal.cn: hand + bag 字面就是「手里的袋」。

normal.en: British handbag equals American purse

normal.en: designer handbag signals luxury
normal.cn: designer handbag（名牌手袋）是奢侈品信号。

normal.cn: handbag 属庞大的 hand 合成词家族。

normal.en: carry, not wear, a handbag

abstract.en: a zipper smiling open over keys

abstract.en: a strap swinging from a bent elbow
abstract.cn: 提带从弯着的手肘荡下。

abstract.en: a queue of bags at an airport scanner

examples.en: She keeps a small umbrella in her handbag.
examples.cn: 她手袋里常备一把小伞。

examples.en: The handbag on sale was half price.

examples.en: Please watch my handbag while I buy tickets.
examples.cn: 我去买票时请帮我看一下手提包。

sensesIntro.en: From a simple carry bag the word rises into fashion, contents, and status.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的随身袋上升到时尚单品、袋中之物与身份象征。

definition_zh: 警告；提醒；告诫；预先通知
definition_en: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
core_image: 一个人伸手拦住同伴，指着前方，要他在踏出下一步之前先停下
scene: 山路边的牌子被风吹得咣咣响，护林员在岔口拦住游客。 He warned us that the path would be icy after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 warn 是「警告、提醒」（第 1 个义项：告知可能发生的危险，以便对方避开）；句意为他提醒我们天黑后小路会结冰。伸手拦住同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：警告、告诫；提醒；预先通知

collocations.zh: 受到警告；要有心理准备

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「警告；警告信号」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已受警告的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「警告者；报警装置」
加前缀 fore- 构成，义为「预先警告」

senses.title: To tell of danger
senses.definition: to tell someone about a danger or problem before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在危险或问题发生之前告诉某人
senses.example: The coastguard warned the boats about the coming storm.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队警告船只将有暴风雨来袭。
senses.why: Old English warnian meant to take heed and to admonish; the word names the act of making someone careful before harm arrives.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 warnian 意为留心与告诫；这个词指在伤害到来之前使人警醒的动作。

senses.title: To advise against
senses.definition: to advise someone strongly not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈劝告某人不要做某事
senses.example: Doctors warn against taking the pills on an empty stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诫不要空腹服用这些药片。
senses.why: The same forward look is aimed at an action: the danger is what the doing would bring, so the advice is a prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对未来的注视，只是这次落在某个动作上：危险正是这个动作会带来的，所以劝告成了禁令。

senses.title: To give notice in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先通知：提前告知某事会来
senses.definition: to inform someone in advance that something is going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知某人某事即将发生
senses.example: Nobody warned me that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人提前告诉我办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: With danger taken out, only the timing remains: the word still speaks of a thing before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 把危险抽掉之后，只剩下时间关系：这个词说的仍是事情发生之前的那一句话。

senses.title: To caution officially
senses.titleCN: 正式警告：由权威出面告诫
senses.definition: to caution a person officially, especially about behaviour or breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 由官方或权威出面告诫某人，尤指其行为或违规
senses.example: The referee warned the player before showing the card.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在出示牌之前先警告了这名球员。
senses.why: An authority repeats the hedge at the cliff edge in a formal voice, and the next step is a penalty.
senses.whyCN: 权威以正式的口吻重演崖边那道拦阻，而下一步就是处罚。

senses.title: To keep someone off
senses.titleCN: 警告离开：阻止某人靠近
senses.definition: in the phrase warn off, to tell someone to stay away from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 warn off，令某人远离某地或某人
senses.example: The farmer warned the walkers off the closed field.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主警告散步的人离开那片封闭的田地。
senses.why: Here the warning becomes a wall of words: the message is not what to watch but where not to stand.
senses.whyCN: 此时警告变成了一道用话砌成的墙：信息不是该注意什么，而是不该站在哪里。

intro.en: Warn comes from an Old English word for refusing or forbidding, and it is close kin to 'beware'.
intro.cn: warn 来自古英语中表示「拒绝、禁止」的词，与 beware 关系很近。

items.en: Warnian meant 'to take heed, be careful', and also 'to admonish or forbid'.
items.cn: warnian 意为「留心、当心」，也表示「告诫、禁止」。

items.en: The noun waru meant 'care, protection, guard', part of the same Germanic cluster.
items.cn: 名词 waru 意为「注意、保护、看守」，属于同一日耳曼词群。

items.en: German warnen 'to warn' and Dutch waarschuwen in part share this history.
items.cn: 德语 warnen 与荷兰语的部分说法共享这段历史。

items.en: The shorter form warn came from the infinitive warnian, and the beware sense drifted to the separate word beware.
items.cn: 较短形式 warn 出自不定式 warnian，而「当心」这一义则漂移到独立词 beware 上。

items.en: The present range runs from a shout at a cliff edge to a formal letter from a court.
items.cn: 现代用法从崖边的呼喊一直到法庭的正式函件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the warn / war shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of telling people about risk.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 warn、war 类词；近义组收告知风险的多种说法。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that tells of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告；警示」，指告知危险的话语或标志。

entries.definition: To be careful of something; the old be-wary sense kept as its own word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「当心」，把古老的「警觉」义保存为独立词。

entries.definition: The past participle of wear, meaning used or damaged; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 wear 的过去分词，意为磨损的；与本词同音，是易混点。

entries.definition: To twist out of shape; an unrelated word of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翘曲、扭曲」，与本词只是形近，来源无关。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be ready for danger; often brief and urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使警觉」，多用于简短紧急的提醒。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be careful, often in a gentler or official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诫」，语气较轻或偏正式。

entries.definition: To state an intention to harm; the warning becomes hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁」，警告在此变成了敌意。

entries.definition: To give someone advice about what to do; warmer and less about danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，语气更和气，重点不在危险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English warnian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 warnian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Warn, not scold: the point is to stop something before it hurts.
normal.cn: warn 不是责骂：要点是在造成伤害之前拦住它。

normal.en: Warn of a thing, warn against an action: the preposition shows the target.
normal.cn: warn of 后接事物，warn against 后接动作：介词显示对象。

normal.en: Beware carries the old careful sense of warn away as its own word.
normal.cn: beware 把 warn 古老的「当心」义带走，成了独立词。

normal.en: A warning can be a word, a sign or a red light.
normal.cn: warning 可以是一句话、一块标志牌或一盏红灯。

normal.en: Worn is a homophone and means used up: do not mix the two.
normal.cn: worn 是同音词，意为磨旧的：不要混用。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff: the body stops first, the explanation comes after.
abstract.cn: 想象在崖边一只手按住同伴的胸口：身体先停下，解释随后才来。

abstract.en: The word faces forward in time: it only works if heard before the harm.
abstract.cn: 这个词朝向未来：只有在伤害之前被听见，它才起作用。

abstract.en: From a shout to a printed notice to a court letter, the same forward-looking alarm.
abstract.cn: 从一声呼喊到一张通告，再到一封法庭来函，是同一种前瞻性的警报。

examples.en: The guide warned us that the bridge might be unsafe.
examples.cn: 导游提醒我们那座桥可能不安全。

examples.en: Doctors warn against skipping breakfast every day.
examples.cn: 医生告诫不要每天都不吃早饭。

examples.en: A red light warns drivers when the crossing is busy.
examples.cn: 人行横道忙碌时，红灯会提醒司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网」——路边拉了红色警示网，提醒你别再往前走：警告

root: 古英语 warnian「留心、告诫、禁止」，与 waru「注意、保护」同属一个日耳曼词群；beware 保存了其中「当心」的一支；派生词有 warning、forewarn。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warn all face forward in time: danger ahead, an action to avoid, news in advance, official caution, and a call to keep away.
sensesIntro.cn: warn 的五个义项都朝向未来：前方的危险、要避开的动作、提前的通告、正式的告诫，以及令人远离的喝止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out against a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一只横在同伴胸前的手。

branches.en: DANGER LINE: the word points at what is coming.
branches.cn: 危险线：这个词指着即将到来的东西。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the advice is aimed at what not to do.
branches.cn: 动作线：劝告落在不该做的事上。

branches.en: NOTICE LINE: the warning may be plain information in advance.
branches.cn: 通知线：警告也可能只是提前告知信息。

branches.en: AUTHORITY LINE: an official voice repeats the same caution.
branches.cn: 权威线：官方声音重复同样的告诫。

branches.en: DISTANCE LINE: warn off pushes the person away.
branches.cn: 距离线：warn off 把人推得更远。

intro.en: Warn is a native verb; its relatives in English are the endings it takes and the beware branch.
intro.cn: warn 是本族动词；它在英语中的亲属是所接的词尾以及 beware 这一分支。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It belongs to the same cluster.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词同属一个词群。

definition_en: the reflexive form of he, used when the object is the same male person as the subject
core_image: 动作转了一圈又落回自己身上
scene: 爸爸平时忙工作，周末独自把婴儿房刷成蓝色，妈妈看了又惊又喜。 He built the bookshelf for the baby room on his own last weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 himself 是「他自己；他亲自」（第 1 个义项：反身用法）；书架是他独立完成的，动作回到自身。

derivatives.zh: 阴性对应反身代词，义为「她自己」
第一人称对应反身代词，义为「我自己」
复数对应反身代词，义为「他们自己」

senses.title: Reflexive: object equals subject
senses.definition: used when the male subject and the object of the verb are the same person
senses.definitionCN: 主语与宾语为同一位男性时使用
senses.example: He taught himself to play the guitar.
senses.exampleCN: 他自学了吉他。
senses.why: The action turns back onto the doer, so the word mirrors he.
senses.whyCN: 动作转回施动者本人，所以这个词是 he 的「镜子」。

senses.title: Emphatic: he did it personally
senses.definition: used to stress that the male person did it personally
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事由他本人亲自完成
senses.example: The manager himself opened the new store.
senses.exampleCN: 经理亲自为新店开业剪彩。
senses.why: Placing himself beside the noun raises that person above others.
senses.whyCN: 把 himself 放在名词旁就把这个人抬了出来。

intro.en: Himself compounds the old dative him with self.
intro.cn: himself 由古老的与格 him 与 self 复合而成。

items.en: Old English used him selfum, meaning to his own self.
items.cn: 古英语有 him selfum，意为「对他自己」。

items.en: The element self has a long Germanic history of self-reference.
items.cn: self 一词在日耳曼语中长期表「自身」。

items.en: Middle English fused the pair into the single form himself.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者融合为 himself 一词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both reflexive and emphatic uses.
items.cn: 现代英语兼有反身与强调两种用法。

items.en: The reflexive family grew: myself, yourself, themselves.
items.cn: 反身代词家族壮大：myself、yourself、themselves。

note.en: Compare himself with the reflexive family.
note.cn: 把 himself 与反身代词家族对照。

entries.definition: reflexive form for women
entries.definitionCN: 阴性反身代词「她自己」

entries.definition: reflexive form for I
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称反身代词「我自己」

entries.definition: reflexive form for they
entries.definitionCN: 复数反身代词「他们自己」

entries.definition: by oneself, without company
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人，与 by himself 义近

entries.definition: done by the person directly
entries.definitionCN: 亲自地，与强调用法义近

entries.definition: without help from others
entries.definitionCN: 独立地，不靠他人

normalIntro.en: Split the word into him + self.
normalIntro.cn: 把 himself 拆成 him + self 记。

normal.en: him + self: the action returns to him.
normal.cn: him 加 self：动作返回到 him 自身。

normal.en: by himself = without any help.
normal.cn: by himself 就是「完全靠自己」。

normal.en: enjoy himself means he has fun.
normal.cn: enjoy himself 就是「他玩得开心」。

normal.en: Himself can shout: The boss himself said so!
normal.cn: himself 能表强调：The boss himself said so!

normal.en: Every pronoun has its self: myself, yourself, himself.
normal.cn: 每个代词都有 self 形式，成套记。

abstract.en: Picture a boomerang flying out and returning to him.
abstract.cn: 想象回旋镖飞出去又回到他手上——反身的画面。

abstract.en: Feel the mirror: the doer and the receiver are one.
abstract.cn: 感受镜子：做者与受者是一人。

abstract.en: See a spotlight jump onto him when himself appears.
abstract.cn: himself 一出现，聚光灯就打到他身上。

examples.en: He repaired the bicycle himself instead of paying for it.
examples.cn: 他自己修好了自行车，没花钱请人。

examples.en: The little boy learned to dress himself this year.
examples.cn: 小男孩今年学会了自己穿衣服。

examples.en: The director himself answered the phone.
examples.cn: 导演亲自接了电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿姆塞夫」——「嘿，他（姆）自己（塞夫）来的」， himself 是「他自己」。

root: himself 由古英语与格 him 加 self（自身）复合而成，本为短语 him selfum「对他自己」，后融合为一个反身代词，属日耳曼语族固有构词。

sensesIntro.en: Himself bends actions back to the doer or lifts him out of the crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: himself 要么把动作弯回施动者自身（反身），要么把这个人从人群中抬起（强调）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the action returning to its own doer
core.cn: 核心意象：动作返回到它自己的发出者

branches.en: object equals the subject
branches.cn: 宾语即主语本人（义项 01）

branches.en: he did it in person
branches.cn: 他亲自完成（义项 02）

branches.en: self-reference built on him
branches.cn: 建立在 him 之上的自指（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: learning or acting alone
branches.cn: 独自学习或行动（义项 01）

branches.en: the person singled out
branches.cn: 被单独点出的人物（义项 02）

intro.en: The self element builds the whole reflexive family.
intro.cn: self 元素构建了整个反身代词家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin uses ipse for the same emphasis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ipse 表达同样的强调。

items.exampleCN: 这个蛋糕是我自己做的。
该规则依事实自动生效。

definition_en: a machine or cabinet that keeps food cold; a large cooling apparatus for storage
core_image: 厨房角落里嗡嗡作响的白色机器，门上贴满便签
scene: 厨房角落那台白色的机器整夜嗡嗡作响，门上贴着孩子的画和几张便签。 She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 refrigerator 是「冰箱」（第 1 个义项：家用冷藏电器）；句意为她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。画面里可留意：白色机器、门上的画与便签、夜里的嗡鸣。

derivatives.zh: 冷藏；冷冻
冷藏；制冷
制冷剂

senses.title: A kitchen appliance
senses.definition: a household cabinet, usually electric, that keeps food cold
senses.definitionCN: 通常用电的、使食物保持低温的家用箱柜
senses.example: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。
senses.why: The Latin name is simply a thing that makes cold, and the kitchen cabinet is the most familiar such thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名称的意思就是「使冷的东西」，而厨房里的箱柜是最为人熟悉的那一个。

senses.title: A large cooling unit
senses.definition: a large machine or room used to keep goods cold in shops or industry
senses.definitionCN: 商店或工业中用来使货物保持低温的大型机器或房间
senses.example: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。
senses.why: The same word serves the home and the trade: both are boxes where cold is made and held.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词家用与商用都管：两者都是制造并保持低温的箱子。

intro.en: Refrigerator is a modern Latin name built from the verb to cool: it means the thing that makes cold.
intro.cn: refrigerator 是用「使冷」的动词构成的近代拉丁名称，意思就是「使冷的东西」。

items.en: Frigus meant cold, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: frigus 意为寒冷，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Frigerare meant to cool something, built on frigus.
items.cn: frigerare 意为使某物变冷，由 frigus 构成。

items.en: Refrigerare added re- and meant to cool down or refresh, often of fevered patients.
items.cn: refrigerare 加上 re-，意为使冷却或使清爽，常用于发热的病人。

items.en: Writers of the nineteenth century formed refrigerator from the verb and the ending -ator, one that does.
items.cn: 十九世纪的写作者用该动词加词尾 -ator（做某事者）造出 refrigerator。

items.en: English applied the name to the ice box, and later to the electric cabinet in every kitchen.
items.cn: 英语先用它指冰柜，后来又指每间厨房里的电动箱柜。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same cooling family; the near-meaning group gathers names for cold storage.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「制冷」词族的词；近义组收表冷藏器具的名称。

entries.definition: To keep something cold.
entries.definitionCN: 冷藏。

entries.definition: The process of cooling.
entries.definitionCN: 制冷；冷藏。

entries.definition: A fluid used in cooling.
entries.definitionCN: 制冷剂。

entries.definition: A household refrigerator.
entries.definitionCN: 冰箱。

entries.definition: A compartment or machine for freezing food.
entries.definitionCN: 冷冻柜。

entries.definition: A container that keeps things cool.
entries.definitionCN: 冷藏箱；冷却器。

entries.definition: An old-fashioned box cooled with ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰柜。

normalIntro.en: The word is literally a cold-maker: a box that produces and holds cold so that food lasts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「造冷者」：一个制造并保持低温、让食物放得更久的箱子。

normal.en: Frigus is cold, and the machine is the thing that makes cold.
normal.cn: frigus 是寒冷，而这台机器就是造冷的东西。

normal.en: Refrigerate the milk, and the refrigerator keeps it cold.
normal.cn: 把牛奶冷藏，冰箱就让它保持低温。

normal.en: The ending ator marks the doer, as in elevator and generator.
normal.cn: 词尾 ator 标记「做某事者」，如 elevator 与 generator。

normal.en: A walk-in refrigerator is big enough to walk inside.
normal.cn: walk-in refrigerator 大到可以走进去。

normal.en: Refrigeration is the process; the refrigerator is the box.
normal.cn: refrigeration 是过程，refrigerator 是箱子。

abstract.en: Cold is not created but moved, and the machine only moves it faster.
abstract.cn: 冷并非被造出，只是被搬运，而机器只是搬得更快。

abstract.en: A refrigerator is a promise that tomorrow will taste like today.
abstract.cn: 冰箱是一个承诺：明天的味道会像今天一样。

abstract.en: The same Latin verb once cooled a fever and now cools a bottle.
abstract.cn: 同一个拉丁动词曾给发热者降温，如今给瓶子降温。

examples.en: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。

examples.en: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
examples.cn: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。

examples.en: Open the refrigerator door and let the cold air out slowly.
examples.cn: 打开冰箱门，让冷气慢慢散出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（加强）加 friger（冷）加 ator（做某事者）：专门造冷的东西，就是冰箱。

root: 拉丁 frigus（寒冷）→ frigerare（使冷）→ refrigerare（使冷却）→ 近代拉丁 refrigerator（造冷者）→ 英语 refrigerator；同族有 refrigerate、refrigeration、refrigerant。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cold-maker; the senses move from the household cabinet to the large cooling room of a shop.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造冷之物」；义项从家用箱柜，到商店里的大型冷藏库。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine humming all night in a kitchen corner, covered with notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房角落里嗡嗡作响、贴满便签的白色机器。

branches.en: milk on a kitchen shelf
branches.cn: 厨房层架上的牛奶

branches.en: a cold room behind a fish shop
branches.cn: 鱼店后面的冷藏室

branches.en: the same cold in a home and a trade
branches.cn: 家中与店里的同一种冷

branches.en: a child's drawing taped to the door
branches.cn: 贴在门上的孩子的画

branches.en: a heavy door that seals a room
branches.cn: 封住房间的厚门

intro.en: A Latin word for cold becomes a verb of cooling, and the agent ending then names the machine that does it.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「寒冷」的词先变成「使冷」的动词，施动者词尾随后命名做这件事的机器。

latinIntro.en: The base is frigus, cold, with frigerare to cool, re- again, and -ator one who does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 frigus（寒冷），frigerare 意为使冷，re- 表「再次」，-ator 指做某事者。

definition_zh: 分开的；单独的；分开；分离
definition_en: not joined together, existing on its own, to divide things, or to move apart
core_image: 一条线把一张纸从中间裁开，两半各自落到桌上
scene: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。 The teacher separated the students into different groups.
sceneCN: 这里 separated 是「分开」（第 3 个义项）；句意：老师把学生分成不同的小组。

derivatives.zh: 分别地
分离
可分开的
不可分开的

senses.title: Not joined
senses.definition: not joined or connected to something else
senses.definitionCN: 没有与其他事物连在一起
senses.example: The twins sleep in separate beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎睡在不同的床上。
senses.why: This is the basic adjective sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的形容词义。

senses.title: On its own
senses.definition: existing or used on its own
senses.definitionCN: 独立存在或单独使用
senses.example: Each room has a separate entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 每个房间都有单独的入口。
senses.why: Being apart makes something distinct.
senses.whyCN: 彼此分开使事物各自独立。

senses.title: To divide
senses.definition: to divide people or things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物分成组
senses.example: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the act of dividing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为分开的动作。

senses.title: To move apart
senses.definition: to move apart or stop living together
senses.definitionCN: 彼此离开或不再共同生活
senses.example: The couple separated last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。
senses.why: People and paths can separate too.
senses.whyCN: 人与道路也可以分离。

intro.en: Separate comes from Latin separare, from se-, apart, and parare, to prepare.
intro.cn: separate 出自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（准备）构成。

items.en: Se- meant apart.
items.cn: se- 意为分开。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or arrange.
items.cn: parare 意为准备或安排。

items.en: Separare meant to set apart.
items.cn: separare 意为使分开。

items.en: English separate covered both the adjective and the verb.
items.cn: 英语 separate 兼作形容词与动词。

items.en: The spelling kept one form for both uses.
items.cn: 拼写保留了两种词性共用的一个形式。

note.en: Separate is compared with similar-looking words and with words for dividing.
note.cn: 把 separate 与形近词以及表示分开的词作比较。

entries.definition: in separate ways
entries.definitionCN: 分别地

entries.definition: the act of dividing
entries.definitionCN: 分离

entries.definition: able to be divided
entries.definitionCN: 可分开的

entries.definition: to split into parts
entries.definitionCN: 分开

entries.definition: to break into pieces
entries.definitionCN: 劈开

entries.definition: clearly different
entries.definitionCN: 截然不同的

normalIntro.en: Separate means set apart, whether as an adjective or an action.
normalIntro.cn: separate 意为使分开，无论作形容词还是动词。

normal.en: The adjective ends with a soft sound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式的结尾发音较轻。

normal.en: The verb ends with the sound of ate.
normal.cn: 动词形式的结尾读作 ate 的音。

normal.en: Separate the white clothes from the dark.
normal.cn: 把浅色衣服与深色衣服分开。

normal.en: They keep separate accounts.
normal.cn: 他们各用各的账户。

normal.en: The couple separated after ten years.
normal.cn: 这对夫妻十年后分居了。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to set it apart.
abstract.cn: 给事物命名，就是把它区分出来。

abstract.en: Some things grow stronger when kept apart.
abstract.cn: 有些事物分开后反而更强。

abstract.en: A line divides the page but joins the story.
abstract.cn: 一条线分开纸页，却连起故事。

examples.en: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
examples.cn: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。

examples.en: Each room has a separate entrance.
examples.cn: 每个房间都有单独的入口。

examples.en: The couple separated last spring.
examples.cn: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。

dict_mnemonic.text: separate 出自拉丁语 separare（使分开），由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，本义「分别安置」，兼作形容词与动词。

root: 源自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，核心义「分别安置」。

sensesIntro.en: Separate means not joined, existing alone, to divide, or to move apart.
sensesIntro.cn: separate 意为分开的、单独的、分开或分离。

core.en: Things set apart from one another.
core.cn: 彼此被分开的事物。

branches.en: Two things no longer joined.
branches.cn: 两个不再相连的物体。

branches.en: One thing standing on its own.
branches.cn: 独立存在的一个事物。

branches.en: The act of dividing a group.
branches.cn: 把一个群体分开的动作。

branches.en: Two people or paths moving apart.
branches.cn: 两个人或两条路彼此远离。

branches.en: Being apart and making apart share one word.
branches.cn: 分开的状态与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Separate belongs to the Latin parare family of preparing and arranging.
intro.cn: separate 属于拉丁语 parare（准备、安排）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin separare and parare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 separare 与 parare 是历史词根。

items.example: The filter is separating the oil.

definition_en: to go back to a place, or to give something back
core_image: 一只鸟沿着熟悉的路线飞回旧巢
scene: 出差一周后，他终于回到了家。 After a week away on business, he finally returned home.
sceneCN: 这里 return 是「返回」（第 1 个义项：回到原来的地方）；句意：出差一周后，他终于回到了家。

derivatives.zh: 可退还的
退回的

senses.title: Go back
senses.definition: to go or come back to a place
senses.definitionCN: 回到原来的地方
senses.example: He returned to his office after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后他回到了办公室。
senses.why: The French source means turn back, so returning is turning one's path around.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为转回，因此 return 就是掉转路程往回走。

senses.title: Give something back
senses.definition: to give something back to its owner or place
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交还给主人或放回原处
senses.example: Please return the key to the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 请把钥匙还到前台。
senses.why: An object that goes back to its owner also makes a return.
senses.whyCN: 物品回到主人手里，也是一种返回。

senses.title: Profit or gain
senses.definition: the profit made from an investment
senses.definitionCN: 投资所带来的利润
senses.example: The investment brought a good return.
senses.exampleCN: 这项投资带来了不错的回报。
senses.why: Money that comes back with more is a return on what was given.
senses.whyCN: 带着更多钱回来的，就是所投入之物的回报。

senses.title: Give in response
senses.definition: to do something for someone because they did it for you
senses.definitionCN: 因对方为你做了什么而回以同样的行为
senses.example: She returned the favor with a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她送了一份礼物来回报这份人情。
senses.why: A favor that comes back to the giver is returned.
senses.whyCN: 回到给予者身上的人情，就是被回报了。

intro.en: Return comes from Old French retorner, to turn back, from re- and torner.
intro.cn: return 源自古法语 retorner（转回），由 re- 与 torner 构成。

items.en: Tornare means to turn.
items.cn: tornare 意为转动。

items.en: Retorner means to turn back.
items.cn: retorner 意为转回。

items.en: Return means come back to a place.
items.cn: return 意为回到某地。

items.en: It also covers giving things back and profit.
items.cn: 它也涵盖归还物品与收益。

items.en: In return marks a response or exchange.
items.cn: in return 标记回应或交换。

note.en: Return is close to come back and give back, and has a financial sense.
note.cn: return 与回来、归还相近，并有金融含义。

entries.definition: sent back
entries.definitionCN: 退回的

entries.definition: able to be given back
entries.definitionCN: 可退还的

entries.definition: to stop working
entries.definitionCN: 退休

entries.definition: to return to a place
entries.definitionCN: 回来

entries.definition: to return something
entries.definitionCN: 归还

entries.definition: money gained in business
entries.definitionCN: 利润

normalIntro.en: Return is a U-turn: you go back the way you came.
normalIntro.cn: return 就是掉头：沿来路走回去。

normal.en: Return home means go back to your house.
normal.cn: return home 意为回到家里。

normal.en: Return a book means give it back to the library.
normal.cn: return a book 意为把书还给图书馆。

normal.en: In return means as a response.
normal.cn: in return 意为作为回应。

normal.en: A return on investment is the profit it makes.
normal.cn: a return on investment 是投资带来的利润。

normal.en: Compare come back: come back is physical, return also covers giving and profit.
normal.cn: 对比 come back：come back 指身体回来，return 还涵盖归还与收益。

abstract.en: Picture a bird flying back to the same nest.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟飞回同一个巢。

abstract.en: Imagine a ball thrown back to the thrower.
abstract.cn: 想象球被扔回投掷者手中。

abstract.en: Think of a coin that comes back with interest.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚带着利息回来的硬币。

examples.en: She returned from the trip on Sunday.
examples.cn: 她星期天旅行归来。

examples.en: He returned the borrowed tools.
examples.cn: 他归还了借来的工具。

examples.en: The shares gave a high return.
examples.cn: 这些股票带来了高回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ turn（转）」——把方向转回来，就是返回；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ tornare（转）→ 古法语 retorner（转回）→ return，核心义「掉转方向往回走」。

sensesIntro.en: Return first means go back, then give something back, then profit that comes back, and finally a response given in exchange.
sensesIntro.cn: return 先指返回，再指归还，再指回到手中的收益，最后指作为交换给出的回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird flying back along a familiar path.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿着熟悉路线飞回的鸟。

branches.en: Going back is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 返回是基本义。

branches.en: Objects also go back to their owners.
branches.cn: 物品也会回到主人处。

branches.en: Money that comes back is a return.
branches.cn: 回来的钱就是收益。

branches.en: A favor given back is returned.
branches.cn: 被回赠的人情就是被回报。

branches.en: Leaving and coming back can be a social exchange.
branches.cn: 离开与回来也可以是一种社交交换。

intro.en: Return is re- plus Latin tornare, to turn.
intro.cn: return 是 re- 加拉丁语 tornare（转）。

latinIntro.en: Latin tornare means to turn, and re- means back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 意为转动，re- 意为回。

items.example: Returnable describes a bottle that can go back.
items.exampleCN: returnable 描述可退回的瓶子。

items.example: Returned describes an item sent back.
items.exampleCN: returned 描述被退回的物品。

definition_zh: 身体的；物质的；物理学的；有形的；需体力的；自然的；（名词）体检
definition_en: relating to the body, to material things, or to physics; existing in a form that can be touched; (noun) a medical examination
core_image: 伸手能摸到、有重量、会疼的那一层世界
scene: 规律的体育活动能让心肺保持强健。 Regular physical activity keeps the heart and lungs strong.
sceneCN: 这里 physical 是「身体的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：规律的身体活动能让心肺保持强健。场景要点：筋骨、出汗、心跳，不是心理层面；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 身体的；物质的；物理学的；有形的；需体力的

forms.label: 比较级（更偏身体／更物质）
最高级（最偏身体／最物质）

derivatives.zh: 身体上；物理上；实在地
物理学
物理学家
体格；体形

senses.title: Relating to the body
senses.titleCN: 身体的：跟筋骨血肉有关
senses.definition: relating to a person's or animal's body rather than the mind
senses.definitionCN: 与人或动物的身体有关，而非与心智有关
senses.example: Regular physical activity keeps the heart and lungs strong.
senses.exampleCN: 规律的身体活动能让心肺保持强健。
senses.why: Greek physis means nature, and the body is the most immediate piece of nature we own. Physical first marked what belongs to the natural, visible self.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 意为“自然”，而身体是我们拥有的最直接的一块自然。physical 最早标记的就是属于这具可见的自然之身的东西。

senses.title: Relating to matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 物质的：由材料构成的那一面
senses.definition: relating to material things and their properties rather than to ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 与物质事物及其属性有关，而非与观念或感受有关
senses.example: The report describes the physical properties of the new alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了这种新合金的物理性质。
senses.why: From the body the word extends to anything that occupies space and can be measured: matter as opposed to meaning.
senses.whyCN: 从身体出发，这个词扩及一切占据空间、可被测量之物：物质，与意义相对。

senses.title: Relating to the science of physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学的：关于力、热、光、电的那门学问
senses.definition: belonging to physics, the science of matter, energy, and their interactions
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理学的，即研究物质、能量及其相互作用的科学
senses.example: Physical chemistry bridges the two departments.
senses.exampleCN: 物理化学把这两个系科连接起来。
senses.why: Physics took its name from the same Greek root. Anything studied by that science is physical in this narrower, technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理学（physics）的名字来自同一个希腊词根。被这门科学研究的东西，就在这个更窄的专业意义上属于 physical。

senses.title: Real and tangible
senses.titleCN: 有形的：真实存在、摸得着
senses.definition: existing in a real, material form that can be touched, seen, or measured
senses.definitionCN: 以真实的、物质的形态存在，可以被触摸、看见或测量
senses.example: The plan finally took physical form as a printed book.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划最终以一本印刷书的实体形态出现。
senses.why: If matter is what can be measured, then 'physical' becomes a guarantee of reality: not imagined, not merely promised.
senses.whyCN: 如果物质就是可被测量的东西，那么 physical 就成了“真实”的保证：不是想象，不只是承诺。

senses.title: Involving bodily force or contact
senses.titleCN: 动身体的：靠力气、会碰撞
senses.definition: involving bodily effort, contact, or force, as in sport or in violence
senses.definitionCN: 涉及身体用力、接触或强制，如体育或暴力场合
senses.example: Ice hockey is a far more physical game than badminton.
senses.exampleCN: 冰球比羽毛球激烈得多，身体对抗也多得多。
senses.why: Bodies in contact is the most visible kind of physical interaction, so the word comes to describe rough, hands-on activity.
senses.whyCN: 身体相互接触是最显眼的物理性互动，所以这个词被用来形容粗重的、动手动脚的活动。

senses.title: Belonging to the natural world
senses.titleCN: 自然的：山川气候，非人造
senses.definition: belonging to nature, especially in contrast with what humans build or arrange
senses.definitionCN: 属于自然界的，尤与人为建造或安排的事物相对
senses.example: Physical geography studies rivers, mountains, and climate.
senses.exampleCN: 自然地理学研究河流、山脉与气候。
senses.why: Physis is nature itself. This sense keeps the oldest meaning most faithfully: whatever is not made by us.
senses.whyCN: physis 就是“自然”。这个义项最忠实地保留了最古老的含义：非由我们制造的一切。

senses.title: Noun: a medical check-up
senses.definition: a medical examination of the body, usually called a physical or a physical exam
senses.definitionCN: 对身体进行的医学检查，通常说 a physical 或 a physical exam
senses.example: She has her annual physical every September.
senses.exampleCN: 她每年九月做一次年度体检。
senses.why: The noun is short for physical examination. The adjective turned into a name for the event in which the body is examined.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 physical examination 的省略。形容词变成了那场“检查身体”的事件之名。

senses.title: Legal: material evidence
senses.definition: in law, referring to objects and traces that can be examined, as opposed to testimony
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指可被检验的实物与痕迹，与证言相对
senses.example: Physical evidence placed him at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 实物证据表明他曾在现场。
senses.why: Courts separate what can be held and tested from what is only said. Physical marks the first category.
senses.whyCN: 法庭把可以拿在手里检验的东西与只是被说出来的话分开。physical 标记的是前一类。

intro.en: Physical descends from the Greek word for nature. Its story is the story of physis: first what grows, then the whole natural order, then the body, then matter itself.
intro.cn: physical 源自希腊语中表示“自然”的那个词。它的历史就是 physis 的历史：先指生长之物，再指整个自然秩序，再指身体，最后指物质本身。

items.en: Phyein meant 'to grow, to bring forth'. It comes from PIE *bheu- 'to grow, to be', the root behind English be and build.
items.cn: phyein 意为“生长、生出”。它来自原始印欧语 *bheu-“生长、存在”，英语 be 与 build 也出自这条根。

items.en: Physis meant 'nature' but literally 'growth'. To the Greeks, a thing's nature was what it grew into when nothing interfered.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然”，字面却是“生长”。在希腊人看来，一物的自然就是它在不受干扰时会长成的样子。

items.en: Physikos meant 'natural, of nature', and also 'about natural things'. It described both the subject matter and the person who studied it.
items.cn: physikos 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“研究自然之物的”。它既描述研究对象，也描述研究的人。

items.en: Latin physicus meant 'natural' and, in later use, 'a physician'. Medieval physica covered medicine and natural philosophy together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physicus 意为“自然的”，后期也指“医生”。中世纪的 physica 把医学与自然哲学合在一起。

items.en: English physical appears in the 16th century with the sense 'of nature'. The sense 'of the body' follows within the same century, and the sense tied to the science of physics develops later.
items.cn: 英语 physical 出现于 16 世纪，意为“自然的”。“身体的”这一义在同一个世纪内跟进；与物理学这门科学相关的义项则更晚发展出来。

items.en: The modern word splits into the body (physical training), matter (physical properties), science (physical chemistry), and reality (physical evidence), all resting on the same Greek idea of nature.
items.cn: 现代这个词分向身体（physical training）、物质（physical properties）、科学（physical chemistry）与实在（physical evidence），全都依托同一个希腊的“自然”观念。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root for nature. The second group collects words for what is bodily or materially real.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示“自然”的希腊词根。第二组收表示“身体的”或“物质上真实”的词。

entries.definition: the science of matter and energy. Greek physika meant natural things; the plural became the name of the science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学。希腊语 physika 意为“自然之物”，其复数形式成了这门学科的名字。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a body. It comes through French from Latin physicus, keeping the bodily focus.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形状与结构。它经法语来自拉丁语 physicus，保留了“身体”这一重心。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. In medieval Latin physicus meant a healer of natural things, that is, the body.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。在中世纪拉丁语里，physicus 指治疗自然之物（即身体）的人。

entries.definition: the study of what lies beyond the physical. Meta- 'after, beyond' plus physics: the books that came after the physics books.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界之外的东西的学问。meta-“之后、超越”加 physics：排在物理学著作之后的那批书。

entries.definition: relating to the body. Bodily overlaps physical in sense 01 but has no material or scientific senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的。bodily 在第 1 义项上与 physical 重叠，但没有物质义或科学义。

entries.definition: made of matter, or concerned with possessions. Material fits sense 02; physical also covers the body and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 由物质构成的，或与财物有关的。material 对应第 2 义项；physical 还覆盖身体与物理学。

entries.definition: having a body. Corporeal is the formal word for sense 01 and is rarely used of objects.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有肉身的。corporeal 是第 1 义项的正式说法，很少用于物体。

entries.definition: able to be touched or clearly perceived. Tangible matches sense 04 and stresses the sense of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 能被触摸或清楚感知的。tangible 对应第 4 义项，强调触觉。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. Natural matches sense 06 and shares the same underlying idea of physis.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、非人造的。natural 对应第 6 义项，底层同样是 physis 的观念。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the body that can be touched, the material object, the physics lab, the printed book, and the sports field.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摸得到的身体、物质对象、物理实验室、印成书的实体、运动场上的对抗。

normal.en: Physical = what you can poke. If your finger stops at it, it is physical.
normal.cn: physical＝你能戳到的东西。手指停在上面的，就是 physical。

normal.en: Physis is nature, and your body is the piece of nature you carry around.
normal.cn: physis 是自然，而你的身体就是你随身携带的那块自然。

normal.en: Physics and physical are the same root: one is the science, the other is what the science studies.
normal.cn: physics 与 physical 同根：一个是学科，一个是这门学科研究的东西。

normal.en: A physical exam is literally a body check: the adjective became the name of the appointment.
normal.cn: a physical exam 字面就是“对身体做的检查”：形容词变成了那次预约的名字。

normal.en: Metaphysics sits after physics: meta- means after, so it is the study of what the physical cannot cover.
normal.cn: metaphysics 排在 physics 之后：meta- 意为“之后”，所以它研究 physical 覆盖不到的部分。

abstract.en: The physical is the layer that resists you; everything else is negotiation.
abstract.cn: 物理层就是会抵抗你的那一层；其余的一切都是协商。

abstract.en: Nature, body, matter, reality: one Greek word supplied four different borders for what counts as real.
abstract.cn: 自然、身体、物质、实在：一个希腊词为“什么算真实”划出了四道不同的边界。

abstract.en: To call something physical is to claim it can be measured; measurement is the modern form of the old word for nature.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 physical，就是声称它可以被测量；测量是那个古老的“自然”一词的现代形态。

examples.en: After the accident he needed months of physical therapy before he could walk unaided.
examples.cn: 事故之后他需要数月的物理治疗，才能独立行走。

examples.en: The two servers are physically separate even though they share one logical name.
examples.cn: 这两台服务器虽然共用一个逻辑名称，物理上是分开的。

examples.en: Detectives found physical evidence that contradicted the witness's account.
examples.cn: 警探找到了与证人陈述相矛盾的实物证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: “菲兹克”听起来像“非此刻”——不是此刻的想法，而是此刻摸得着的东西：physical 物质的、身体的

root: 希腊语 phyein“生长”→ physis“自然（生长之物）”→ physikos“自然的”→ 拉丁 physicus → 英语 physical；与 physics、physique、physician、metaphysics 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Everything here comes from one Greek word for nature. The body is nature closest to us; matter is nature outside us; physics is nature studied; a physical exam is the body inspected; physical evidence is reality that can be handled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这里的一切都出自一个表示“自然”的希腊词。身体是离我们最近的自然；物质是我们之外的自然；物理学是被研究的自然；体检是被检查的身体；实物证据是可以拿在手里的实在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing against a solid surface and feeling it push back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在坚实表面上，感到它顶回来。

branches.en: BODY: the natural self and the examination of it.
branches.cn: 身体：自然的自身，以及对它的检查。

branches.en: MATTER: material properties, tangible reality, and evidence that can be handled.
branches.cn: 物质：物质属性、可触摸的实在、可拿在手里的证据。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the department that studies matter and energy.
branches.cn: 科学：研究物质与能量的那门学科。

branches.en: FORCE: bodies in contact, effort and collision.
branches.cn: 力：身体相触，用力与碰撞。

branches.en: NATURE: the non-human world, kept closest to the Greek original.
branches.cn: 自然：非人造的世界，最贴近希腊原义。

intro.en: The family rests on the Greek noun for nature and its adjective. English adds the usual endings for sciences, persons, and properties.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语表示“自然”的名词及其形容词上。英语加上表示学科、人物与性质的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed physicus and physica, and through them the root reached medicine before it reached physics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入 physicus 与 physica，这条词根先进入医学，后才进入物理学。
