definition_zh: 世纪；一百年；百年（板球中击球员的一百分）
definition_en: a period of one hundred years; a hundred runs scored by one batsman
core_image: 一本厚厚的大书，每一页是一年，一册就是一百年
scene: 全家翻看旧相册，照片里的曾祖母还是个小女孩。 My great-grandmother was born in the last century.
sceneCN: 这里 century 是「世纪」（第 1 个义项：一百年）；句意是曾祖母出生于上个世纪。

derivatives.zh: 由 cent 构成，义为「百年纪念」
由 cent 构成，义为「百岁老人」
由 century 加 old 构成，义为「百年之久的」

senses.title: A period of one hundred years
senses.definition: any stretch of time lasting one hundred years
senses.definitionCN: 任何持续一百年的时间段
senses.example: The school has a history of one century.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校有一百年历史。
senses.why: The cent- root means hundred, so a century is one hundred years.
senses.whyCN: cent- 词根意为「百」，所以 century 就是一百年。

senses.title: One of the numbered hundred-year periods
senses.definition: a hundred years counted from a fixed year, as in the 21st century
senses.definitionCN: 从某一年起算的一百年，如二十一世纪
senses.example: Printed books spread fast in the fifteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷书籍在十五世纪迅速传播。
senses.why: History needed big boxes for time, so centuries got numbers.
senses.whyCN: 历史需要给时间分大格子，世纪便被编上号。

senses.title: A hundred runs in cricket
senses.definition: one hundred runs scored by a single batsman in cricket
senses.definitionCN: 板球中一名击球员获得的一百分
senses.example: He scored a century in his first match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在首场比赛就得了一百分。
senses.why: One hundred of anything can borrow the hundred-word.
senses.whyCN: 无论什么，达到一百都可以借用这个「百」词。

intro.en: Century is Roman army talk that grew into a word for time.
intro.cn: century 原是罗马军队用语，后来变成时间的词。

items.en: Latin centuria was a group of one hundred soldiers, and also a division of land.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centuria 指百人队，也是一种土地划分单位。

items.en: It came from centum, the Latin word for a hundred.
items.cn: 它源自 centum，即拉丁语的「一百」。

items.en: English borrowed century in the sixteenth century, first for groups of a hundred things.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 century，最初指「一百个一组」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it mainly meant a hundred years of time.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它主要指一百年时间。

items.en: In sports reporting it later named a batsman's hundred runs.
items.cn: 在体育报道中，它后来又指击球员的一百分。

note.en: The hundred-family and other time words.
note.cn: 「百」家族与其他时间词。

entries.definition: one hundredth of a dollar
entries.definitionCN: 分（美元的百分之一）

entries.definition: one hundredth of a metre
entries.definitionCN: 厘米

entries.definition: out of every hundred
entries.definitionCN: 百分之……

entries.definition: a person of a hundred years old
entries.definitionCN: 百岁老人

entries.definition: a period of ten years
entries.definitionCN: 十年

entries.definition: a period of one thousand years
entries.definitionCN: 千年

entries.definition: a long period marked by something special
entries.definitionCN: 时代

entries.definition: a period of history
entries.definitionCN: 时代；年代

normalIntro.en: century = cent + -ury: the hundred word.
normalIntro.cn: century = cent 加 -ury：「百」之词。

normal.en: cent- means hundred, from Latin centum.
normal.cn: cent- 意为百，来自拉丁语 centum。

normal.en: a century is one hundred years.
normal.cn: 一个世纪是一百年。

normal.en: decade has ten years, century has a hundred.
normal.cn: decade 是十年，century 是一百年。

normal.en: the 21st century began in the year 2001.
normal.cn: 二十一世纪始于二〇〇一年。

normal.en: in cricket, a century is one hundred runs.
normal.cn: 板球中 century 指一百分。

abstract.en: Picture a very old tree that has watched a whole century.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵见证整整一个世纪的老树。

abstract.en: Picture a dusty bookshelf holding one book for each century.
abstract.cn: 想象落灰的书架，每个世纪放一本书。

abstract.en: Picture a batsman raising his bat after one hundred runs.
abstract.cn: 想象击球员在一百分后高举球板。

examples.en: The temple was built more than a century ago.
examples.cn: 这座庙建于一个多世纪前。

examples.en: Mobile phones changed life within a single century.
examples.cn: 手机在一个世纪内改变了生活。

examples.en: Historians call the years 2001 to 2100 the 21st century.
examples.cn: 历史学家把二〇〇一年到二一〇〇年称为二十一世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森雀」——森林里的麻雀活了一百年还在开会，那可是整整一个世纪，所以「森雀」= century。

root: 拉丁语 centum（一百）→ centuria（百人队）→ 英语 century。与 cent（分）、percent（百分之）、centimetre（厘米）同根。

sensesIntro.en: From rows of soldiers to blocks of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 从士兵队列到时间块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hundred of something
core.cn: 核心意象：一百之数

branches.en: One hundred years of time
branches.cn: 一百年时间

branches.en: Numbered periods of history
branches.cn: 编号的历史时期

branches.en: A cricket milestone
branches.cn: 板球里程碑

branches.en: Long change over time
branches.cn: 漫长时间中的变化

branches.en: Books, wars and turning points
branches.cn: 书籍、战争与转折点

intro.en: Cent- words all carry the number one hundred.
intro.cn: cent- 系列词都带着「一百」这个数字。

latinIntro.en: Latin centum is the number at the heart of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum 是词族核心的数字。

items.example: A century has one hundred years.
Ninety percent agreed with the plan.
items.exampleCN: 百分之九十的人同意该计划。

items.example: The town threw a centennial party.

items.exampleCN: 我的邻居是位百岁老人。

items.example: The city celebrates its bicentennial next year.
items.exampleCN: 该市明年庆祝建城两百周年。

latinEntries.meaning: a body of one hundred soldiers

definition_zh: 必要的；必需的；必然的；必需品（常用复数 necessaries）
definition_en: needed so that something can be done or achieved; certain to happen as a result; and, as a plural noun, the things a person needs
core_image: 一把钥匙插进锁孔，门后是缺了它就办不成的那件事
scene: 出发前一晚，队长把清单摊在木桌上逐项核对，缺了任何一样队伍都走不成。 A map and a compass are necessary for the route they have chosen.
sceneCN: 这里「necessary」是「必要的、必需的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就无法完成某事）；句意是地图和指南针是他们所选路线必需的装备。图中可辨识物件：木桌上的清单、地图、指南针。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性；必需品」
由 necessary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「必然地」
由 necessary 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不必要的」

senses.title: Needed for a purpose
senses.definition: required so that something can happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而不可缺少的
senses.example: Water is necessary for every living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 水对每个活细胞来说都是必需的。
senses.why: Latin necessarius first meant what cannot be avoided; English moved that force into the practical sphere, where it marks what cannot be left out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necessarius 最初指躲不开的东西；英语把这份强制感移进日常事务，用来标出不能漏掉的那一项。

senses.title: Certain to follow as a result
senses.definition: certain to happen as a result of something else, with no real alternative
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的结果必定发生，没有别的可能
senses.example: A rise in temperature is a necessary result of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 温度上升是这场反应的必然结果。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, it can also be called necessary as a consequence: the cause leaves the effect no room to differ.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既躲不开，也就可以作为结果被称为必然：原因没给结果留下任何差异的余地。

senses.title: Things a person cannot do without
senses.definition: the items a person needs for daily life, usually used in the plural form
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活离不开的物品，通常用复数形式
senses.example: The family packed only the necessaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人只收拾了过冬最基本的必需品。
senses.why: An adjective turns into a noun when English wants to name the objects that carry the quality; the plural marks a set of such objects rather than one.
senses.whyCN: 当英语想直接称呼带有这种性质的物件时，形容词就变成名词；复数标记的是一整套这样的东西，而不是单件。

intro.en: Necessary reached English through French from Latin, and its root idea is not simply wanted but impossible to avoid.
intro.cn: necessary 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，它的根义不是「想要」，而是「避不开」。

items.en: Behind the Latin word lie a negative particle and a root for yielding, though the exact prehistoric form is not settled.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示退让的词根，但更早的确切形式尚无定论。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable; one widely repeated account divides it into ne, not, and cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免；一种流传很广的解释把它分成 ne（不）与 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without and passed both necessity and practical need to later languages.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 指离不开的东西，把「必然」与「实际需要」一起传给了后世语言。

items.en: Old French necessaire carried the word to England after the Norman conquest, where it was spelled in several ways.
items.cn: 古法语 necessaire 在诺曼征服后把这个词带到英格兰，当时拼写有好几种。

items.en: Modern English uses necessary for what is required and for what must follow, and the plural noun for the bare items of daily life.
items.cn: 现代英语用 necessary 既指「必需」也指「必然」，复数名词则指日常生活里最基本的那些东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Latin stem and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what cannot be done without.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干及其词尾展开；近义组收表示「缺了就不行」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb formed from necessary with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The state of being necessary, or a thing that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必需品。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: Not needed; more than is required.
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的；多余的。

entries.definition: Absolutely needed for something to exist or work.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或运作绝对需要的。

entries.definition: Needed for life or for success.
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的。

entries.definition: Demanded by a rule or by the situation.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或情形所要求的。

entries.definition: Too important to be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到不可缺少的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin refusal to yield, put to work in shopping lists, rules and consequences; the family keeps that double life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是拉丁语里「不肯退让」的劲头，后来被用在清单、规则和结果上，同族词一直保留这双重身份。

normal.en: Necesse carries the sense of what will not give way, which is why necessary can mean both required and certain.
normal.cn: necesse 带着「不肯让步」的意味，所以 necessary 既能指「必需」，也能指「必然」。

normal.en: The plural noun necessaries is old-fashioned but correct for a set of daily needs.
normal.cn: 复数名词 necessaries 虽显旧，但指一整套日常所需时是正确的。

normal.en: Unnecessary adds un-, and the word simply reverses: not needed rather than needed.
normal.cn: unnecessary 加了 un-，词义直接反转：不是必需，而是不必要。

normal.en: Necessity names the state, necessitate the act, and necessary the quality, all from one Latin base.
normal.cn: necessity 指状态，necessitate 指动作，necessary 指性质，三者同出一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: If necessary is a fixed phrase that shortens a whole conditional clause into two words.
normal.cn: if necessary 是固定说法，把一个完整条件句压缩成两个词。

abstract.en: A key that opens one door is necessary only because of that door; the word always implies a purpose behind the need.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙之所以必需，是因为有那扇门；这个词背后总藏着一个目的。

abstract.en: A necessary result is a consequence with no side road, which is why the same adjective can sound like fate.
abstract.cn: 必然结果是一条没有岔路的结果，所以同一个形容词有时听起来像命运。

abstract.en: Calling things necessaries reduces a whole life to a short list of objects that must be carried.
abstract.cn: 把东西叫作 necessaries，等于把一整段生活压缩成一张必须携带的短清单。

examples.en: The repair is necessary before the bridge can reopen.
examples.cn: 桥要重新开放，先得完成这项维修。

examples.en: Sleep is necessary for the body to recover.
examples.cn: 睡眠对身体恢复是必要的。

examples.en: The shelter kept only the bare necessaries for the night.
examples.cn: 收容所只留了过夜最基本的必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞瑞」——必需品总在「呢色」堆里被翻出来；记住 necessary 是必要的、必然的。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由 ne-（不）与 cedere（退让）构成，派生形容词 necessarius；经古法语 necessaire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what cannot be done without; the senses then split into practical need, forced consequence, and the plural noun for the objects themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「缺了就不行」；义项分出实际需要、被迫产生的结果，以及直接指物件本身的复数名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turning in a lock that will not open without it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙插进锁孔，没有它就打不开那扇门。

branches.en: a checklist with one item circled twice
branches.cn: 清单上有一项被圈了两遍

branches.en: a thermometer rising because the reaction has started
branches.cn: 反应开始后温度计一路上升

branches.en: a suitcase holding only soap, thread and a candle
branches.cn: 行李箱里只有肥皂、线团和一支蜡烛

branches.en: a bridge waiting for one last repair before traffic
branches.cn: 桥等着最后一项维修才放行

branches.en: a shop shelf marked for daily needs
branches.cn: 货架上标着日常所需的那一排

intro.en: A Latin negative, a verb of yielding, an adjective and two English endings build this entry from the inside out.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁否定成分、一个表示退让的动词、一个形容词和两个英语词尾，从内到外搭起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is well recorded: necesse, its derived adjective necessarius, and the verb cedere that the negative element is thought to contain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基有明确记载：necesse、由它派生的形容词 necessarius，以及一般认为藏在否定成分里的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 主要地；首要地；大部分地；大体上
definition_en: chiefly, above all; for the most part
core_image: 一屋子的人里，绝大多数都举着同一种颜色的旗子
scene: 散场后，清洁工推着车穿过空荡的展厅，地上留下的东西并不多。 The mess left behind was mainly paper cups and torn programmes.
sceneCN: 这里表示「大部分是」（第 2 个义项：大部分地）；句意为留下的垃圾主要是纸杯和撕破的节目单。

pos.zh: 主要地；首要地；大部分地

derivatives.zh: mainly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词与名词，义为「主要的；主管道」
由 main 与 stream 复合，义为「主流」
由 main 与 stay 复合，义为「支柱」

senses.title: Above all; chiefly
senses.definition: more than anything else, when the point is what matters most
senses.definitionCN: 在强调最重要的原因或因素时，表示「首要地、主要地」
senses.example: The delay was mainly caused by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 延误主要是风暴造成的。
senses.why: Main means chief, and -ly turns that judgement into an adverb: mainly marks the factor that outweighs the rest.
senses.whyCN: main 意为首要的，-ly 把这个判断变成副词：mainly 标出压过其余因素的那一个。

senses.title: For the most part
senses.definition: in most cases or to most of a group, when the point is quantity or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 在强调数量或比例时，表示「大部分、多数情况下」
senses.example: The audience was mainly students from nearby schools.
senses.exampleCN: 观众大部分是附近学校的学生。
senses.why: The same adverb can measure a group instead of ranking a cause, so mainly also means that most members share the trait being named.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词也可以衡量一个群体，而不是给原因排序，所以 mainly 还表示多数成员都具有所说的特征。

intro.en: Mainly is the adjective main fitted with the old adverb suffix -ly, and main itself goes back to a Germanic noun for strength.
intro.cn: mainly 是形容词 main 加上古老的副词后缀 -ly 构成，而 main 本身可追溯到日耳曼语表示力量的名词。

items.en: The base is mægen, a noun for strength or force.
items.cn: 基础词是 mægen，一个表示力量或威力的名词。

items.en: The reconstructed *maginam is the common Germanic source of mægen and of might.
items.cn: 重构形式 *maginam 是 mægen 与 might 共同的日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English main took the sense chief or principal from that root.
items.cn: 中古英语 main 从这一词根取得「首要、主要」的意思。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly, from Old English -līce, was added to main to make mainly.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 源自古英语 -līce，加在 main 后构成 mainly。

items.en: Modern English uses mainly for both the leading cause and the largest share of a group.
items.cn: 现代英语里 mainly 既指首要原因，也指群体中的最大部分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on main; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of majority and chief importance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 main 构成的形式；近义组收表示多数与首要地位的副词。

entries.definition: Chief or principal; also a principal pipe or supply.
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；也指主管道或公共供应。

entries.definition: The principal land mass, as opposed to islands.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于岛屿而言的主要陆地；大陆。

entries.definition: Ideas or practices accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被多数人接受的思想或做法；主流。

entries.definition: The chief support of a system or group.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或群体的主要支柱。

entries.definition: In most cases or to the greatest degree.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下；大部分地。

entries.definition: Above all; mainly.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地；主要地。

entries.definition: To a great extent; mostly.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上；大部分。

entries.definition: Mainly; in the majority.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；占多数地。

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds -ly to a word for strength and chief weight, so it can rank a cause or measure a majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词把 -ly 加在表示力量与首要分量的词后，因此既能给原因排序，也能衡量多数。

normal.en: Mainly is main plus -ly, so the adverb keeps the idea of ranking: one thing outranks the rest.
normal.cn: mainly 是 main 加 -ly，所以这个副词保留了排序的意思：某样东西压过其余。

normal.en: The -ly ending comes from Old English -līce, which turned a quality into a manner of acting.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾来自古英语 -līce，把某种性质变成行事的方式。

normal.en: When mainly points at a cause, it works like chiefly; when it points at a crowd, it works like mostly.
normal.cn: 当 mainly 指向原因时，它相当于 chiefly；当它指向一群人时，它相当于 mostly。

normal.en: The word is a judgement about weight, so mainly does not mean only; other factors can still be present.
normal.cn: 这个词是对分量的判断，所以 mainly 不等于 only，其他因素仍可能存在。

normal.en: Mainly because and mainly due to are the two phrases that show the adverb ranking a reason.
normal.cn: mainly because 与 mainly due to 是展示这个副词给原因排序的两个短语。

abstract.en: A hall where nearly everyone holds the same colour of flag: the crowd shows what mainly means.
abstract.cn: 满厅几乎人人举着同一种颜色的旗子：人群本身就展示了 mainly 的意思。

abstract.en: To say what mainly caused something is to put one weight on the scale and let the others stay lighter.
abstract.cn: 说出某件事主要因何而起，就是在一杆秤上放一个更重的砝码，让其余都轻一些。

abstract.en: Ranking and proportion are two faces of one adverb, both asking which part deserves the emphasis.
abstract.cn: 排序与比例是同一个副词的两张脸，两者都在问哪一部分值得强调。

examples.en: The delay was mainly caused by the storm.
examples.cn: 延误主要是风暴造成的。

examples.en: The audience was mainly students from nearby schools.
examples.cn: 观众大部分是附近学校的学生。

examples.en: The mess left behind was mainly paper cups and torn programmes.
examples.cn: 留下的垃圾主要是纸杯和撕破的节目单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹利」——主要靠小妹出力；记住 mainly 是主要地。

root: main（主要的）加副词后缀 -ly；main 源自日耳曼语表示「力量」的词根，同族词有 might、may，无可靠拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is ranking by weight; it splits into the leading cause and the largest share of a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是按分量排序；义项分成首要原因与群体中的最大部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale with one heavy weight tipping it down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杆秤，一端放着最重的那块砝码。

branches.en: one heavy weight tipping the scale
branches.cn: 一块重砝码压得秤面倾斜

branches.en: a crowd where nearly every flag is the same colour
branches.cn: 几乎每面旗都是同一种颜色的人群

branches.en: ranking a cause and counting a majority under one adverb
branches.cn: 用一个副词既给原因排序，也数出多数

branches.en: a sentence naming the storm first
branches.cn: 一句话把风暴放在最前

branches.en: a list where most names come from one town
branches.cn: 名单上多数名字来自同一个镇

intro.en: The word is held together by the Germanic noun for strength, its adjective main, and the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语表示力量的名词、它的形容词 main，以及副词后缀 -ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the family is Germanic, reaching back to a noun for strength.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，这一族属于日耳曼语，源自一个表示力量的名词。

definition_zh: 物理学；物理；（口语）事物的物理特性与运作原理
definition_en: the science of matter, energy, motion and the forces that govern them, or the physical way something works
core_image: 一只摆锤从最高点落下，旁边并排放着温度计、磁铁与棱镜，都在量同一件事：物体如何运动与相互作用
scene: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，试图用同一条定律解释两种现象。 In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究物质、运动与相互作用的物理学」，对应第 1 个义项：作为一门学科的整体；句意为学生用同一条物理定律解释单摆与透镜两种现象。画面要点：摆锤、温度计、磁铁、棱镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 物理学（不可数，作学科名称；口语中也可指某物的运作机制）

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）
形而上学（表示「之后、超越」的前缀与物理学复合，原指编在物理学之后的讨论，后指研究存在本身的学问）

senses.title: The science of matter and motion
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与运动的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, forces and the structure of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量、运动、力以及宇宙结构的那门科学
senses.example: In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，希望同一条物理定律能解释两者。
senses.why: The Greek source named 'natural things', so the discipline begins as the study of whatever happens by nature rather than by human arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「自然之物」，因此这门学科起初研究的是依本性而非依人造安排发生的一切。

senses.title: How a particular thing works
senses.titleCN: 某具体事物的运作原理
senses.definition: the physical principles behind a device, a sport or a natural event
senses.definitionCN: 某个装置、某项运动或某种自然现象背后的物理原理
senses.example: The coach explained the physics of a spinning ball.
senses.exampleCN: 教练讲解了旋转球的物理原理。
senses.why: The name of a whole discipline can be applied to one small case, because every case is an instance of the same laws.
senses.whyCN: 整门学科的名称可以用在一个小案例上，因为每个案例都是同一批定律的实例。

senses.title: Classical mechanics in practice
senses.definition: the part of the subject dealing with bodies moving well below the speed of light, as formulated before relativity
senses.definitionCN: 研究远低于光速运动的物体、在相对论之前已成体系的那部分内容
senses.example: The bridge design was checked with classical physics.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁设计用经典物理作了校核。
senses.why: The old core of the subject kept the plain name, so 'physics' often means the mechanics of ordinary speeds and sizes.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科旧有的核心保留了这个朴素的名字，因此「物理」常指日常速度与尺度下的力学。

senses.title: Relativity and the quantum
senses.titleCN: 相对论与量子层面的现代物理
senses.definition: the parts of the subject that describe very fast, very massive or very small systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述极快、极重或极小系统的那部分内容
senses.example: Modern physics begins where the classical laws stop working.
senses.exampleCN: 现代物理从经典定律失效之处开始。
senses.why: When the old laws failed at the extremes, the same word had to cover the theories that replaced them.
senses.whyCN: 当旧定律在极端情形下失效，同一个词就必须覆盖取而代之的新理论。

senses.title: Branch subjects built on the name
senses.titleCN: 以该词构成的各分支学科
senses.definition: fields formed by joining a prefix to the subject, such as the physics of stars, of the earth or of living things
senses.definitionCN: 在学科名称前加前缀构成的领域，如研究星体、地球或生物的那几门
senses.example: Astrophysics applies the methods of physics to stars.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理把物理学的方法用于星体。
senses.why: A method that works on one scale invites use on every scale, so the name becomes a suffix for whole new fields.
senses.whyCN: 在一个尺度上有效的方法会被用到所有尺度，于是这个名字成了新领域的后缀。

senses.title: A course and a textbook
senses.titleCN: 一门课程与一本教科书
senses.definition: the school or university subject as it is taught, examined and written up
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里被教授、考核与编写成书的那门科目
senses.example: She took physics in her first year and chemistry in her second.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一年修物理，第二年修化学。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a subject when it acquires a syllabus, and the same noun then names the room, the hour and the book.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问获得教学大纲后就成了科目，同一个名词于是也命名教室、课时与课本。

senses.title: The mechanism behind an outcome
senses.definition: the practical cause-and-effect chain that makes something happen, used in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的实际因果链条，用于日常口语
senses.example: The physics of the market is not the same as the physics of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的运作机制与桥梁的运作机制并不相同。
senses.why: Speakers borrow the word whenever they want to say that something has a mechanism rather than a mystery.
senses.whyCN: 说话者借用这个词，是想说某事有一套机制，而不是一个谜。

senses.title: Natural philosophy in older use
senses.definition: the older name for the study of nature, before the modern sciences separated
senses.definitionCN: 现代各门科学分化之前，研究自然的学问的旧称
senses.example: Newton wrote his great work under the old name for physics.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿以物理学的旧称写下他的巨著。
senses.why: Before disciplines divided, the study of nature was one subject, and its old title is still visible in the word's ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 在各学科分化之前，对自然的研究是一门学问，它的旧称仍可见于这个词的来历。

intro.en: Physics comes from Greek phusis 'nature', through Latin physica 'natural things'. English first used physic for medicine, and later took physics for natural science, so the two forms parted company.
intro.cn: physics 出自希腊语 phusis「自然」，经由拉丁语 physica「自然之物」传入。英语先用 physic 指医学，后来用 physics 指自然科学，两种形式从此分道。

items.en: Phuein 'to grow, bring forth' is the verb at the root of the family, and it describes what comes into being by itself.
items.cn: phuein 意为「生长、产生」，是这个词族的根动词，描述自行生成之物。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, as opposed to what is made by craft.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，与人以技艺造作之物相对。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises on nature, and the phrase became the name of the subject.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德论自然诸篇的标题，这个说法后来成为学科名称。

items.en: Latin physica, a neuter plural, named natural science, and it passed into English in that form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 是中性复数，指自然科学，并以这一形式进入英语。

items.en: In English physic first meant the art of healing, because medicine studied the natural body; that sense survives in the word for a doctor.
items.cn: 在英语中，physic 起初指医术，因为医学研究的是自然身体；这一意思残留在表示医生的那个词里。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the plural form was used for natural science, while the singular stayed with medicine. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，复数形式用来指自然科学，单数形式则留在医学。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature but has split into medicine, body build and the adjective; the second group places the subject among neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，但已分成医学、体格与形容词；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的科学之中。

entries.definition: The art of healing, now archaic; it is the same source word, but it named medicine rather than the science of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 医术，现已古旧；它是同一个来源词，但命名的是医学，而不是研究物质的科学。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a person's body; it comes from the same Greek root but through French, and names a frame rather than a field.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形态与力量；它出自同一希腊词根，但经法语传入，命名的是体格而不是学科。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body, as opposed to the mental; it describes a kind of thing, while the entry word names a science.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的，与心理的相对；它描述一类事物，而本词命名一门科学。

entries.definition: A person trained in the subject; the suffix marks the practitioner rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 受过该学科训练的人；后缀标示从业者，而不是领域。

entries.definition: Any science of the physical world, including biology, chemistry and geology; the entry word is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界的任何科学，包括生物学、化学与地质学；本词是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of bodies and the forces acting on them; it is a branch of the entry subject rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物体及作用其上的力；它是本学科的一个分支，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: Sciences of non-living systems, such as physics and chemistry; the phrase is broader and excludes biology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究非生命系统的科学，如物理与化学；这个说法更宽，但不包括生物学。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge obtained by observation and experiment; it covers every discipline, of which the entry word is one.
entries.definitionCN: 经观察与实验获得的系统知识；它覆盖所有学科，本词是其中之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the Latin plural for natural things, real derived words and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、拉丁语中表示「自然之物」的复数、真实派生词与真实分支名称。

normal.en: The root means nature, so the subject begins as the study of what happens by itself.
normal.cn: 词根意为「自然」，因此这门学科起初研究自行发生之事。

normal.en: The family runs physical, physically, physicist, astrophysics and metaphysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理的、身体上、物理学家、天体物理与形而上学。

normal.en: The older singular meant medicine, which is why a doctor and a scientist share a root.
normal.cn: 较早的单数形式指医学，所以医生与科学家共有一个词根。

normal.en: The subject splits into classical and modern halves, and into branches named by a prefix.
normal.cn: 这门学科分成经典与现代两半，也分成由前缀命名的各分支。

normal.en: A pendulum and a lens obey the same laws, which is the promise the word makes.
normal.cn: 单摆与透镜服从同一批定律，这正是这个词所许诺的事。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum at the top of its arc, a thermometer beside it and a prism splitting light, all waiting to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摆锤停在弧线的最高点，旁边是温度计，还有一块分光的棱镜，都在等着被测量。

abstract.en: Picture a single law written on a card, held up against two completely different experiments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片上写着一条定律，被举到两组完全不同的实验面前。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose trunk is nature and whose branches are named after stars, rocks and living cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，树干是「自然」，枝干则以星体、岩石与活细胞命名。

examples.en: The physics of the atmosphere explains why the balloon rose so fast.
examples.cn: 大气的物理原理解释了气球为何上升得那么快。

examples.en: He studied physics before turning to the history of science.
examples.cn: 他先修物理，后来转向科学史。

examples.en: No law of physics forbids the machine, only the cost does.
examples.cn: 没有物理定律禁止这台机器，只是成本不允许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹克斯」——「费」力气去「测」：摆锤、棱镜、温度计，量的都是同一件事，这就是物理。

root: 希腊语 phuein「生长、产生」→ phusis「自然」→ ta phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics。较早的英语形式 physic 指医学，后复数形式专指自然科学；这一分开的年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings radiate from one discipline. The subject itself comes first, then the practical physics of a single thing, then its classical core, its modern extensions, its branch subjects, its life as a course, its looser use for any mechanism, and its older name as natural philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一门学科辐射开。先是学科本身，其次是某件具体事物的运作原理，再其次是它的经典内核、现代扩展、各分支学科、作为课程的存在、泛指任何机制的宽松用法，以及它作为「自然之学」的旧名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swinging pendulum beside instruments that all measure the same interaction.
core.cn: 核心意象：摆动的摆锤，旁边是一同测量同一种相互作用的仪器。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the whole discipline, and the same thing as a course and a textbook.
branches.cn: 学科：整体学问，以及它作为课程与教科书的存在。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: how one thing works, and the everyday use of the word for any causal chain.
branches.cn: 机制：某物如何运作，以及日常口语中用这个词泛指任何因果链。

branches.en: CLASSICAL CORE: bodies at ordinary speeds, governed by the older laws.
branches.cn: 经典内核：日常速度下的物体，由较早的定律支配。

branches.en: MODERN EDGE: what happens at extreme speed, mass or smallness.
branches.cn: 现代边缘：在极端速度、质量或微小尺度下发生的事。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND ANCESTOR: prefix-named fields, and the older single study of nature.
branches.cn: 分支与祖先：以前缀命名的各领域，以及较早的那门统一的自然之学。

intro.en: The family comes from a Greek verb for growing, through a Greek noun for nature and a Latin plural for natural things; English then built adjectives, persons and whole branch names on it.
intro.cn: 这个词族出自一个表示「生长」的希腊动词，经由表示「自然」的希腊名词与表示「自然之物」的拉丁复数，英语再在其上构成形容词、人物名词与整批分支名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below are themselves borrowed from Greek; they carried the subject into English and also left the older word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式本身借自希腊语；它们把这门学科带入英语，也留下了表示医学的那个较早的词。

items.meaning: the science of matter and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与运动的科学
items.example: Physics explains why the apple falls.
items.exampleCN: 物理学的解释了苹果为何下落。

items.example: The physical world obeys measurable laws.
items.exampleCN: 物质世界服从可测量的定律。
这项任务对体力要求很高。

items.example: The physicist measured the decay rate.
items.exampleCN: 那位物理学家测量了衰变率。

items.meaning: the art of healing, now archaic
items.example: The old physic book lists herbal remedies.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列着草药方。

items.meaning: the physics of stars and space
items.meaningCN: 研究星体与太空的物理
items.exampleCN: 天体物理研究恒星如何形成。

items.example: Geophysics maps the rock beneath the city.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理测绘城市地下的岩层。
生物物理为蛋白质折叠建立模型。

items.meaning: the study of being, placed after the physical treatises
items.meaningCN: 研究存在的学问，原编排在物理诸篇之后
items.example: The question belongs to metaphysics, not to physics.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于形而上学，而不是物理学。

latinEntries.structure: physica, physicorum (n., neuter plural, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）

definition_en: to feel concern and interest, or the attention and work given to protect someone or something
core_image: 双手捧着易碎的东西，轻轻护住
scene: 下雨了，同桌把伞往我这边挪了挪。 My deskmate shifted her umbrella towards me to show how much she cared.
sceneCN: 这里 care 是「关心；在意」（第 1 个义项：心里挂念对方）；句意为同桌挪伞给我，以示关心。

derivatives.zh: 由 care 加 -ful 构成，义为「小心的；仔细的」
由 care 加 -less 构成，义为「粗心的」
与 care 同源相关，义为「职业；生涯」

senses.title: To feel concern for someone
senses.definition: to feel that someone or something matters to you
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某人某物对你是要紧的
senses.example: She really cares about her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她真心关心朋友们。
senses.why: Old English caru meant a heavy mind full of worry, and worry grows where something matters.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 caru 指满怀忧虑的心，而忧虑正是因对方要紧而生。

senses.title: To look after someone or something
senses.definition: to do what is needed to keep someone healthy, safe and well
senses.definitionCN: 做让某人健康安全所需之事
senses.example: The nurse cares for the patients every day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天照料病人。
senses.why: When a matter sits heavy in the mind, the hands follow with daily tending.
senses.whyCN: 心里挂着的事，手上便有了日常的照料。

senses.title: Attention to avoid mistakes
senses.definition: attention and effort to avoid harm or error
senses.definitionCN: 避免伤害或出错的用心
senses.example: Handle the glass with care.
senses.exampleCN: 拿玻璃杯要小心。
senses.why: A worried mind moves slowly and checks twice, which is exactly carefulness.
senses.whyCN: 挂心的心走得很慢、再三核对，这正是「小心」。

intro.en: Care began as an old word for a heavy, worried mind.
intro.cn: care 起初是古词，指沉重忧愁的心。

items.en: A Germanic root meaning grief or burden stands behind the word.
items.cn: 日耳曼语源词根意为悲伤或重负。

items.en: Old English caru meant sorrow, anxiety and burden of mind.
items.cn: 古英语 caru 指悲伤、忧虑与心头的负担。

items.en: Middle English kept the worry sense and added taking charge of someone.
items.cn: 中古英语保留忧虑义，又添「替人担起责任」之义。

items.en: Dutch zorg and German Sorge are cousins with the same worry sense.
items.cn: 荷兰语 zorg 与德语 Sorge 是表亲，同含忧虑之义。

items.en: Modern English stressed warm concern, daily tending and carefulness.
items.cn: 现代英语强调温暖的关切、日常照料与谨慎。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects concern-and-tending neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收关切与照料类词。

entries.definition: A road vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汽车」，拼写与 care 接近。

entries.definition: The central part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「核心」，拼写与 care 相近。

entries.definition: To make an illness go away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「治愈」，拼写与 care 接近。

entries.definition: To feel anxious about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「担忧」，与 care 的旧义相近。

entries.definition: To matter to someone; interest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「关切」，近于 care 的关心义。

entries.definition: To look after someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「照料」，近于 care 的照顾义。

normalIntro.en: Remember care through its old worry root.
normalIntro.cn: 借古老的忧虑词根记忆 care。

normal.en: care began as a mind heavy with worry.
normal.cn: care 起初指心事重重的忧虑。

normal.en: care about someone means they matter to you.
normal.cn: care about 即对方对你要紧。

normal.en: take care is the everyday goodbye.
normal.cn: take care 是日常道别语。

normal.en: careful adds -ful, full of care.
normal.cn: careful 加 -ful，满是小心。

normal.en: careless drops the care with -less.
normal.cn: careless 用 -less 把「心」丢了。

abstract.en: Picture two hands cupped around a small flame in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在风中拢住一簇小火苗。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders lighten when someone asks if you are all right.
abstract.cn: 被人问一句「还好吗」，肩膀松了下来。

abstract.en: See a nurse checking on each bed in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象护士逐床查看的画面。

examples.en: Mum told me to take care on the icy road.
examples.cn: 妈妈叮嘱我在结冰的路上小心。

examples.en: He cares about the stray cats near school.
examples.cn: 他关心学校附近的流浪猫。

examples.en: Grandpa needs someone to care for him now.
examples.cn: 爷爷现在需要有人照顾他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯儿」——心里挂着那个凯旋的孩儿，时时关心。

root: 原始日耳曼语词根（悲伤、重负）→ 古英语 caru（忧虑）→ 中古英语 care（忧虑；照管）→ 现代英语 care；德语同族 Sorge（忧虑）。

sensesIntro.en: Care moves from a worried mind to warm concern, daily tending and careful handling.
sensesIntro.cn: care 从忧心出发，长出关切、照料与谨慎诸义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something heavy resting on the heart
core.cn: 核心意象：压在心头的一件挂念之事

branches.en: Feeling that someone matters
branches.cn: 觉得对方要紧

branches.en: Daily looking after
branches.cn: 日常的照料

branches.en: Handling things gently
branches.cn: 轻拿轻放的谨慎

branches.en: Friendship and family warmth
branches.cn: 亲情友情的温度

branches.en: Doing the work of protection
branches.cn: 履行保护之事

intro.en: Care is a plain root whose endings build a whole family of words.
intro.cn: care 是个朴素词根，接上后缀便长成整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Care has no Latin source; its family grows on Germanic endings.
latinIntro.cn: care 无拉丁语源，其词族靠日耳曼后缀生长。

items.example: Care sat on her mind all night.
Be careful with the hot soup.
A careless error cost the point.
He drove carefully in the rain.

items.meaning: a running course, then a life's work
one who takes care of a place

items.example: A carefree afternoon in the park.
items.exampleCN: 公园里无忧无虑的下午。

definition_zh: 图案；模式；规律；纸样；范例；（动词）仿照；以图案装饰
definition_en: a repeated design or a regular arrangement; a model to copy; also a verb meaning to model something on another or to decorate with a design
core_image: 一个方块被刻成印版，压到布上，再压一次、又一次，同样的形状排成一片
scene: 裁缝铺的长桌上摊开一张纸样，粉笔线在布面上勾出重复的方格， The tailor pins the paper pattern onto the cloth before cutting.
sceneCN: 这里 pattern 指「裁剪用的纸样模板」（第 3 个义项：供复制用的样板）；句意为裁缝把纸质样板别到布上再下剪。图中可辨识物件：长桌、纸样、粉笔线、别针与格纹布面。

derivatives.zh: 有图案的；按模式排列的
图案形成；模式化

senses.title: A repeated decorative design
senses.definition: a design of repeated shapes, lines or colours used to decorate a surface
senses.definitionCN: 由重复的形状、线条或色彩构成、用于装饰表面的图样
senses.example: The curtains carry a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘上带着细小的花卉图案。
senses.why: The word began as patron, 'a model to copy'; decoration repeats a copied unit across a surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初借自意为「可复制的范本」的外来词；装饰正是把一个被复制的单元铺满表面。

senses.title: A recurring sequence of events
senses.definition: a regular and repeated way in which events or actions occur
senses.definitionCN: 事件或行为有规律地反复出现的方式
senses.example: The patient's sleep pattern changed after the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行之后，这位患者的睡眠规律变了。
senses.why: Once a model is repeated in time rather than on a surface, the repetition itself becomes the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当范本不是铺在表面、而是在时间中反复，重复本身就成了模式。

senses.title: A template or model for making copies
senses.titleCN: 供复制使用的样板或模板
senses.definition: a shape or model used as a guide for cutting, sewing or casting
senses.definitionCN: 裁剪、缝制或浇铸时用作依据的形状或模型
senses.example: She pinned the paper pattern to the fabric and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 她把纸质样板别到布上，沿粉笔线剪开。
senses.why: This is the literal ancestor: a pattern is first an object you lay down and copy.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的祖先义：pattern 最初就是一件可以铺下来照着复制的东西。

senses.title: The arrangement of parts that forms a whole
senses.definition: the way elements are arranged or organized in a whole
senses.definitionCN: 各要素在整体中被排列或组织的方式
senses.example: The novel's pattern of images returns in the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中那组意象的排列在最后一章再次出现。
senses.why: From a copied outline the sense broadens to any arrangement whose parts answer one another.
senses.whyCN: 从可复制的轮廓出发，词义扩展到任何部件彼此呼应的排列。

senses.title: A regularity detected in data or nature
senses.titleCN: 在数据或自然中找出的规律
senses.definition: a recognizable regularity in measurements, behaviour or natural forms
senses.definitionCN: 在测量、行为或自然形态中可辨认的规律性
senses.example: The software looks for patterns in the sales figures.
senses.exampleCN: 软件在销售数据中寻找规律。
senses.why: Science makes the repetition an object of search: the pattern is the order found in what looked random.
senses.whyCN: 科学把重复变成搜寻的对象：模式就是从看似随机之物里找出的秩序。

senses.title: A recurring arrangement in language
senses.titleCN: 语言中反复出现的结构
senses.definition: a regular arrangement of sounds or words that speakers of a language follow
senses.definitionCN: 说某种语言的人所遵循的、语音或词句的规律性排列
senses.example: The drill fixes the sentence pattern in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 反复操练把句型固定在记忆里。
senses.why: Language is learned through repeated shapes, so the same word names the frames a speaker reuses.
senses.whyCN: 语言通过反复的形状被学会，同一个词便用来命名说话者反复套用的框架。

senses.title: A model of conduct held up for imitation
senses.definition: an example or model of behaviour that others are expected to follow
senses.definitionCN: 他人应当效仿的行为榜样或范例
senses.example: The older teachers were held up as a pattern of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年长的教师被举为耐心的典范。
senses.why: This restores the Latin model sense: patronus was a protector and an exemplar, and pattern kept that moral use into modern English.
senses.whyCN: 这恢复了拉丁语的范本义：patronus 既是保护人也是榜样，pattern 把这一道德用法保留到现代英语。

senses.title: To model something on, or decorate with a design
senses.definition: to make or shape something according to a model, or to decorate a surface with a regular design
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个范本制作或塑造某物，或以规则图样装饰表面
senses.example: The garden was patterned on a larger estate in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是仿照北方一处更大的庄园建造的。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: whatever follows a model is patterned on it, and a surface given a repeated design is patterned too.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：照着范本做的，就是依范本而制；被赋予重复图样的表面也可说带图样的。

intro.en: Pattern comes from Middle English patron, taken from Latin patronus 'protector, model', which was built on pater 'father'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pattern 来自中古英语的借形，后者出自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」，而 patronus 由 pater「父亲」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pater meant 'father'. It is the base of patronus and also of English words about fatherhood and protection.
items.cn: pater 意为「父亲」。它既是 patronus 的词基，也是一批表示父系与保护的英语词的来源。

items.en: The suffix -onus built nouns of role or function; added to pater it produced patronus, 'one who acts as a father to others'.
items.cn: 后缀 -onus 构成表示角色或职能的名词；加在 pater 上便产生 patronus，意为「替他人承担父职的人」。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, defender' and, in later Latin, 'a model or example to be followed'.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、辩护者」，在后期拉丁语中又指「可供效法的范本或榜样」。

items.en: English took patron through Old French, where it kept both the protector and the model senses.
items.cn: 英语经由古法语接受这个借形，古法语同时保留了保护人与范本两种含义。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling shifted from patron to pattern, and the 'model' sense moved to the centre of the word.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，拼写最终定为 pattern，「范本」义逐渐成为这个词的核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: why the written form settled as pattern rather than patron is not fully explained; sixteenth-century spelling habits are generally assumed to be the cause.
items.cn: 来源不确定：书写形式为何最终定为 pattern 而非较早的借形，尚无完满解释；一般认为与 16 世纪的拼写习惯有关。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close to pattern, including its own ancestor; the second holds words for design and for models to copy, which differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 pattern 的词，其中包含它自己的祖先形式；第二组指图案与可复制的范本，各自强调的方面不同。

entries.definition: A person who supports or protects someone; this is the form English borrowed first, before pattern took over the model sense.
entries.definitionCN: 支持或保护他人的人；这是英语最先借入的形式，后来 pattern 才承担了范本义。

entries.definition: An official right to an invention; from Latin patere 'to lie open', with no link to pater 'father'.
entries.definitionCN: 对发明享有的官方专有权；来自拉丁语 patere「敞开」，与 pater「父亲」无关。

entries.definition: A wooden shoe or clog worn to raise the foot above mud; it only sounds like pattern and has no shared sense with it.
entries.definitionCN: 垫高脚步以免陷入泥中的木鞋或木套鞋；只是读音像 pattern，意义并无交集。

entries.definition: The planned arrangement of lines, shapes or colours; design can be invented rather than repeated, while pattern stresses repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 对线条、形状或色彩的规划性安排；设计可以原创而不必重复，pattern 则强调重复。

entries.definition: One repeated figure within a design; a motif is the unit that a pattern repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 图案中反复出现的单个图形；母题正是被图案重复的那个单元。

entries.definition: A shaped guide for cutting or drawing; it is the physical model sense of pattern, without the decorative senses.
entries.definitionCN: 裁剪或描画用的成形样板；它就是 pattern 的实体范本义，不含装饰性的义项。

entries.definition: A thing or person taken as an example to copy; model is wider and also covers scale models and abstract systems.
entries.definitionCN: 被拿来照着做的物或人；model 范围更广，还包括缩比模型与抽象系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Pattern began as patron, a model to copy.
normal.cn: pattern 最初借自一个意为「可照抄的范本」的外来词。

normal.en: A pattern repeats one unit across a surface, like a stamp pressed again and again.
normal.cn: 图案是把一个单元铺满表面，像印章一次次压下去。

normal.en: The paper pattern in a sewing shop is a model laid on cloth.
normal.cn: 裁缝铺里的纸质样板，就是铺在布上的模型。

normal.en: Weather patterns repeat in time, not on a wall.
normal.cn: 天气模式在时间中重复，而不是在墙上重复。

normal.en: Pattern recognition is the search for order in what first looks random.
normal.cn: 模式识别就是在初看杂乱之处寻找秩序。

abstract.en: Picture a single tile copied until the whole floor becomes a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一块瓷砖被不断复制，直到整个地面成为一个故事。

abstract.en: Picture a river that cuts the same bend every year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河每年都切出同一个弯。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence frame that many different words can step into.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子框架，许多不同的词都能走进去。

examples.en: The tiles form a geometric pattern across the floor.
examples.cn: 瓷砖在地面上构成几何图案。

examples.en: Doctors noticed a pattern in the patients' symptoms.
examples.cn: 医生们注意到患者的症状中有一种规律。

examples.en: The new school was patterned on a design from the coast.
examples.cn: 这所新学校是仿照沿海地区的一个设计建造的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派藤」——藤条编出的格子一遍遍重复，派上去铺满就成图案。patron 本是「范本」，照着范本一次次复制，就有了 pattern。

root: 中古英语的借形来自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」；patronus 由 pater「父亲」加名词后缀 -onus 构成。拼写后来变为 pattern，「范本、样板」义成为核心，再引申出图案、模式与规律等义。拼写变化的具体原因属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a repeated decorative design, then move to a sequence in time and a model cut from paper, to arrangement and detected regularity, to language and moral example, and end with the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从重复的装饰图案开始，转到时间中的次序与纸质样板，再到部件排列与被找出的规律，再到语言结构与道德典范，最后是动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one unit is stamped, cut or copied again and again, so repetition itself becomes the visible order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个单元被反复压印、裁剪或复制，重复本身成了可见的秩序。

branches.en: THE REPEATED UNIT: the core sense is a copied shape repeated across a surface until the surface is covered.
branches.cn: 重复的单元：核心义是一个被复制的形状在表面上反复出现，直到铺满。

branches.en: REPETITION IN TIME OR ON PAPER: a habit repeats on a schedule, and a template is the model laid down before the copy is made.
branches.cn: 在时间中或在纸上的重复：习惯按时间表反复，样板则是复制之前铺下的模型。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND ORDER: the word widens from a visible design to the way parts fit a whole, and then to a regularity found in data.
branches.cn: 排列与秩序：词义从可见图样扩展到部件构成整体的方式，再扩展到数据中被找出的规律。

branches.en: A SHAPE OTHERS COPY: a sentence frame is reused by speakers, and a moral example is held up for others to follow.
branches.cn: 被别人复制的形状：句型被说话者反复套用，道德榜样则被举出来供人效法。

branches.en: THE ACTION OF COPYING: the noun becomes a verb, so a thing can be patterned on a model or patterned with a design.
branches.cn: 复制的动作：名词转为动词，于是可以说某物仿照某个范本，或表面被赋予图样。

intro.en: Pattern can be read as a Latin noun base, a Latin role suffix and the English word that grew out of them, plus two adjective endings.
intro.cn: pattern 可以读作一个拉丁名词词基、一个拉丁角色后缀、由它们生长出来的英语词，再加两个形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater 'father' with -onus produced patronus 'protector, model'; English shortened it to patron, respelled it pattern, and later added -ed and -less.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater「父亲」加 -onus 构成 patronus「保护人、范本」；英语先缩略这个词形，再改写为 pattern，后来又加两个词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The noun supplies the family image behind the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供拉丁词背后的家族意象。

items.meaning: one who acts in a role or function
items.meaningCN: 承担某种角色或职能的人
items.example: The suffix turns 'father' into a word for one who protects others.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「父亲」变成表示保护他人者之词。

items.example: Latin used the noun for a protector and later for an example.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指保护人，后来也指榜样。

items.example: English kept the older form beside its respelled doublet.
items.exampleCN: 英语把较旧的形式与改写后的同源词并存在一起。

items.structure: pattern (English noun and verb, respelled from patron)
items.meaning: a repeated design; a model to copy
items.meaningCN: 重复的图案；可复制的范本
items.example: The respelled form took over the model and design senses.
items.exampleCN: 改写后的形式承接了范本与图案两种含义。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective of possession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示拥有的形容词。

items.meaning: having a pattern; modelled on something
items.example: The fabric is patterned with small squares.
items.exampleCN: 这块布上有小方格图案。

items.example: The suffix removes the quality the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀去掉名词所指的性质。

derivatives.meaning: the noun of design shifts to an adjective meaning 'provided with a pattern' or 'modelled on something'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由表示图案的名词转为形容词，表示「带有图案」或「仿照某物」

derivatives.meaning: the noun shifts to an adjective meaning 'having no pattern'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由名词转为形容词，表示「没有图案的」

definition_en: the flavour of food, the ability to judge what is good, or to try food with the tongue
core_image: 舌尖刚碰到一勺热汤
scene: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。 She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
sceneCN: 这里 taste 是「品尝」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。

derivatives.zh: 美味的
有品位的
无味的；不得体的

senses.title: The flavour of food
senses.definition: the flavour that food or drink has in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 食物或饮料在口中呈现的滋味
senses.example: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。
senses.why: The core sense is what the tongue reports about food.
senses.whyCN: 核心义项是舌头对食物作出的报告。

senses.title: To try food
senses.definition: to put food or drink in the mouth to find out its flavour
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或饮料放入口中以辨别滋味
senses.example: She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
senses.exampleCN: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。
senses.why: The noun became the act of testing flavour.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成了检验滋味的动作。

senses.title: Good judgment of style
senses.definition: the ability to judge what is beautiful or suitable
senses.definitionCN: 判断美与得体的能力
senses.example: Her taste in music is very wide.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐上的品味很广。
senses.why: Judging flavour by the tongue became judging quality by the mind.
senses.whyCN: 用舌头判断滋味，扩展为用头脑判断品质。

senses.title: A small experience of something
senses.definition: a short experience that shows what something is like
senses.definitionCN: 让人了解某事滋味的短暂经历
senses.example: He had a taste of success at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁时初尝成功的滋味。
senses.why: A taste is a small sample, and an experience can be sampled too.
senses.whyCN: 品尝本就是取一小口，人生经历也可以「取一小口」。

intro.en: Taste came from a word meaning to touch and test, not only to eat.
intro.cn: taste 源自「触摸、检验」之词，最初并不只与吃有关。

items.en: Taxare meant to touch sharply and judge.
items.cn: taxare 意为触击并评判。

items.en: Taster meant to touch and try.
items.cn: taster 意为触摸并试验。

items.en: Tasten meant to try food in the mouth.
items.cn: tasten 意为在口中试食物。

items.en: Taste extended to judgment of style.
items.cn: taste 扩展到对风格的判断。

items.en: It also means a small experience.
items.cn: 它还表示短暂的体验。

note.en: Taste is compared with look-alike words and with words for flavour and preference.
note.cn: 把 taste 与形近词以及表示滋味和偏好的词作对比。

entries.definition: having a good flavour
entries.definitionCN: 美味的

entries.definition: showing good judgment
entries.definitionCN: 有品位的

entries.definition: an examination
entries.definitionCN: 测试；只拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the taste of food
entries.definitionCN: 风味

entries.definition: to test something
entries.definitionCN: 尝试

entries.definition: a liking for one thing
entries.definitionCN: 偏好

normalIntro.en: Taste began with touching and testing, then settled on the tongue.
normalIntro.cn: taste 从触摸与检验开始，最后落在舌头上。

normal.en: She tasted the soup and found it salty.
normal.cn: 她尝了汤，觉得有点咸。

normal.en: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
normal.cn: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。

normal.en: Her taste in music is very wide.
normal.cn: 她在音乐上的品味很广。

normal.en: He had a taste of success at nineteen.
normal.cn: 他十九岁时初尝成功。

normal.en: That joke was in poor taste.
normal.cn: 那个玩笑不得体。

abstract.en: Tasting is testing with the tongue.
abstract.cn: 品尝就是用舌头检验。

abstract.en: Style is flavour judged by the mind.
abstract.cn: 品味是头脑评判的风味。

abstract.en: A small taste can teach a whole life.
abstract.cn: 一小口滋味能教会整个人生。

examples.en: She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
examples.cn: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。

examples.en: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
examples.cn: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。

examples.en: Her taste in music is very wide.
examples.cn: 她在音乐上的品味很广。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忒斯特」——舌尖「忒」地碰到汤，立刻判断出滋味，就是品尝。

root: 拉丁语 taxare（触击、评判）经古法语 taster（触摸、试验）进入英语，由「检验」转为「品尝」。

sensesIntro.en: Taste moves from testing by touch to flavour on the tongue, then to judgment and brief experience.
sensesIntro.cn: taste 从触摸检验，到舌尖滋味，再到判断力与短暂体验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tongue meeting the edge of a spoon.
core.cn: 核心意象：舌尖碰到勺子的边缘。

branches.en: Flavour is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 滋味是日常义项。

branches.en: Tasting is the testing act.
branches.cn: 品尝是检验的动作。

branches.en: Judgment grows from testing.
branches.cn: 鉴赏力从检验中长出。

branches.en: A taste is a small sample of life.
branches.cn: 体验是人生的一小口。

branches.en: Both mean taking a sample.
branches.cn: 两者都表示取一点样本。

intro.en: Taste builds -y, -ful, and -less adjectives.
intro.cn: taste 构成 -y、-ful、-less 三个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare, to touch and judge, underlies taste through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 taxare（触击评判）经古法语构成 taste 的词源。

definition_en: to press something so that it moves away from you; to urge someone to act; to promote a product or idea; also a strong coordinated effort to achieve something
core_image: 两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽
scene: 货车在坡道上熄了火，司机跳下来，绕到车尾，双手抵住厢板。 He pushed hard until the wheels began to turn.
sceneCN: 这里 push 是「用力推」（第 1 个义项：施加力量使物体移动）；句意为他一直用力推，直到车轮开始转动。画面里可留意：货车、坡道、车尾厢板。

derivatives.zh: push 加表人后缀 -er，指推的人，口语中也指贩毒者
push 加 -y 构成形容词，指过分急于达到目的、咄咄逼人的
push 与 up 复合，指靠双臂把身体撑起的俯卧撑
push 与 back 复合，指推回去的力量，现多指反对与抵制

senses.title: To press something away from you
senses.definition: to press a person or thing so that it moves away from you or moves forward
senses.definitionCN: 按住人或物，使它离开你或向前移动
senses.example: He pushed the door open with one shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一边肩膀把门顶开了。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word meant to beat or drive, so the earliest English sense is a hand or a body driving an object forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词本义是击打、驱赶，所以英语最早的义项就是用手或身体把东西向前顶开。

senses.title: To urge someone to act
senses.definition: to urge or pressure someone to do something, especially when they are slow or unwilling
senses.definitionCN: 催促或施压让某人去做某事，尤指对方迟缓或不情愿时
senses.example: The teacher pushed the class to finish before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 老师催全班在中午前做完。
senses.why: A hand can move a thing, and the same force can be applied to a person's will, so physical pressure becomes social pressure.
senses.whyCN: 手能推动物体，同样的力气也能加到人的意愿上，于是身体的推变成了人际的催逼。

senses.title: To promote a product or idea
senses.definition: to try hard to sell a product or to make an idea accepted by many people
senses.definitionCN: 努力卖出产品，或让某个想法被许多人接受
senses.example: The company pushed its new phone through every channel it had.
senses.exampleCN: 公司用尽所有渠道推销它的新手机。
senses.why: Selling is moving goods towards buyers, so the verb for moving an object forward was borrowed for moving goods out of the shop.
senses.whyCN: 销售就是把货物推向买家，于是「把东西往前推」的动词被借来指把货推出店门。

senses.title: A determined campaign or advance
senses.definition: a planned and forceful effort to achieve something, or a military advance
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某事而组织起来的一次有力行动，或军事上的推进
senses.example: The union began a push for shorter hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会开始了一场争取缩短工时的行动。
senses.why: Beside the verb grew a noun: the whole forward movement, repeated by many hands, became a single campaign with a name.
senses.whyCN: 动词旁边长出了名词：许多人一次次向前使力，整体就成了有名字的一场行动。

intro.en: Push came from Old French pousser, whose Latin ancestor pulsare meant to beat or strike repeatedly; the same Latin family also gave English pulse and compel.
intro.cn: push 来自古法语 pousser，其拉丁语祖先是 pulsare（反复击打）；同一拉丁词族还给英语带来了 pulse 与 compel。

items.en: Pellere meant to drive, strike or set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of Latin verbs of movement.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱动、击打、使动，是拉丁语一大批运动动词的共同源头。

items.en: Pulsare was a frequentative of pellere, meaning to beat or knock again and again, as a hand does on a door.
items.cn: pulsare 是 pellere 的反复动词，意为一下一下地击打，像手在门上敲个不停。

items.en: Old French pousser meant to push or thrust and is the form English borrowed; the older spelling poulser is also recorded.
items.cn: 古法语 pousser 意为推、顶，英语借的正是这个形式；文献中还有更早的拼写 poulser。

items.en: English attests pushen in the thirteenth century, at first for bodily shoving and soon for pressing an argument or a claim.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪已见 pushen，起初指身体上的推搡，很快也用于推进某个论点或主张。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to advertising, queues, prices and campaigns, while the noun keeps the sense of one coordinated forward movement.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到广告、排队、价格与竞选，名词则保留「一次协同的向前推进」之意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin root of beating and driving; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「击打、驱动」词根上的词；近义组收其他表示用力移动某物的动词。

entries.definition: To beat or throb with a regular rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律地跳动、搏动。

entries.definition: A single beat of the heart or of a regular wave.
entries.definitionCN: 心脏或规律波动的一次搏动。

entries.definition: To force someone to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某人做某事。

entries.definition: To drive something back or keep it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物击退或挡开。

entries.definition: To push someone or something roughly.
entries.definitionCN: 粗暴地推人或推物。

entries.definition: To push gently, often with the elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻一推，常指用手肘碰。

entries.definition: To drive something forward with sudden force.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地向前推送。

entries.definition: To push steadily against something.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地压、按。

normalIntro.en: The word descends from a Latin verb of beating, and its senses all keep the picture of force applied at one point.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示击打的动词，各个义项都保留着「在一点上使力」的画面。

normal.en: Pellere drives and pulsare beats; push is the repeated beat that finally moves the object.
normal.cn: pellere 是驱动，pulsare 是反复击打；push 就是那一下下敲击终于把东西推动了。

normal.en: Old French pousser is the direct source, which is why push looks nothing like its Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: 古法语 pousser 是直接来源，所以 push 的拼写与它的拉丁祖先毫无相似之处。

normal.en: Pushy adds -y to the action and turns it into a personality that keeps pressing other people.
normal.cn: pushy 在动作后加 -y，把「推」变成一种不断对别人施压的性格。

normal.en: A push-up is the body lifting itself by pushing down on the floor.
normal.cn: push-up 是靠向下推地面把身体撑起来的动作。

normal.en: Pushback is the force that returns when you push, now used mostly for people resisting a plan.
normal.cn: pushback 是你推出去之后返回来的一股力，如今多指人们对某项计划的抵制。

abstract.en: Force applied at one point can move a whole object, which is why the word suits hands, campaigns and markets alike.
abstract.cn: 作用在一点上的力能移动整个物体，所以这个词既能用于手，也能用于运动和推广。

abstract.en: A society moves forward when someone grows tired enough of standing still to start pushing.
abstract.cn: 社会往前动，往往是因为有人厌倦了原地不动，开始使力。

abstract.en: Pushing and pulling are the two directions of every bargain, and most deals settle somewhere between them.
abstract.cn: 推与拉是每场讨价还价的两种方向，多数交易最终落在两者之间。

examples.en: She pushed the heavy box across the floor.
examples.cn: 她把那只沉重的箱子推过地板。

examples.en: The campaign pushed hard for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 这场运动为争取更清洁的空气大力施压。

examples.en: One final push got the team over the line.
examples.cn: 最后一次发力让队伍越过了终点线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「布什」——布什总统一挥手，把前面的人往前一推，记住 push 是推。

root: 古法语 pousser（推）← 拉丁语 pulsare（反复击打）← pellere（驱动、击打）；同族有 pulse、compel、repel。

sensesIntro.en: The core is force applied at a point; the senses divide into moving an object, pressing a person, selling goods, and one organized forward effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是在一点上使力；义项由此分为推动物体、催逼他人、推销货物，以及一次有组织的推进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms flat against a heavy door, the gap widening by a finger's width.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽。

branches.en: a palm flat against a stuck door
branches.cn: 一只手掌平贴在卡住的门上

branches.en: a hand on someone's back at the start line
branches.cn: 起跑线上按在他人后背的手

branches.en: a new phone in every window display
branches.cn: 每个橱窗里都摆着的新手机

branches.en: a march moving one field closer
branches.cn: 向前推进一地的行军

branches.en: pressure that moves a person and a whole group
branches.cn: 推动一个人也推动一群人的力量

intro.en: The word is held together by two Latin verbs of driving and beating, an Old French verb, and English suffixes that make a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个表示驱动与击打的拉丁动词、一个古法语动词，以及构成「人」与「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: too eager to get what one wants
items.meaningCN: 过分急于得到；咄咄逼人的

definition_zh: 愉快；快乐；乐事；消遣；荣幸
definition_en: a feeling of happiness or enjoyment, and also the thing or activity that produces it
core_image: 夏夜院子里，一把旧藤椅和一杯凉茶带来的松弛
scene: 忙完一整天，老人把藤椅搬到院子里坐下，长长舒了口气。 The cool evening air gave her a quiet pleasure after a long day.
sceneCN: 这里指的是「愉快、快乐」这种心情（第 1 个义项）；句意为傍晚的凉风让劳累一天的她在心里松了下来。画面里有院子、藤椅和渐暗的天色。

pos.zh: 愉快；快乐；乐事；消遣；荣幸

derivatives.zh: 由 pleasure 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的」
由 pleasurable 加 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地」
由 pleasure 与 seeking 复合而成，义为「追求享乐的」

senses.title: A feeling of happiness
senses.definition: a feeling of happiness, enjoyment or satisfaction that comes from something agreeable
senses.definitionCN: 由合意之事带来的高兴、享受或满足的感受
senses.example: He listened to the rain with quiet pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 他安静地听着雨声，心里很愉快。
senses.why: The noun comes from the same Latin verb as please, so it names the feeling that is left behind once something has been agreeable to you.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词与 please 同出拉丁语 placere（使愉快），因此它指的是某样东西合你心意之后，留在你心里的那份舒服。

senses.title: Something that gives enjoyment
senses.definition: an activity, event or object that gives you enjoyment and can be counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 能带来愉快、可以一件件数出来的活动、事件或物件
senses.example: Her garden is her greatest pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 她的花园是她最大的乐事。
senses.why: Once the feeling has a name, the countable thing that produces it borrows the same word, so a garden or a trip can itself be called a pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 心情先有了名字，接着产生这种心情的具体事物也沿用同一个词，于是一座花园、一趟旅行本身就能叫 pleasure。

senses.title: Enjoyment rather than work
senses.definition: enjoyment taken from an activity done for its own sake, not for duty or money
senses.definitionCN: 从只为本身而做的活动中得到的享受，不为职责或报酬
senses.example: He reads history for pleasure, not for exams.
senses.exampleCN: 他读历史是为了消遣，不是为了考试。
senses.why: Because the word already means enjoyment itself, adding the phrase for pleasure marks an activity as done only to obtain that enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就指享受，所以 for pleasure 一出现，就等于声明这件事只为得到享受而做，不为别的。

senses.title: A courteous formula of willingness
senses.definition: used in polite formulas to say that you are glad to help or glad to have met someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于客套话，表示乐于帮忙或很高兴与某人相识
senses.example: It was a pleasure to work with such a careful team.
senses.exampleCN: 能和这样细致的团队共事是一件愉快的事。
senses.why: In social formulas the feeling is offered to the other person, so the word turns into a courteous way of saying that helping costs you nothing.
senses.whyCN: 在客套话里，这份愉快被送给对方，于是这个词变成一种礼貌表态：帮你这件事对我来说并不构成负担。

intro.en: Pleasure and please share one Latin source; the noun came into English through French and settled as the general word for enjoyment.
intro.cn: pleasure 与 please 共有一个拉丁源头；名词经法语进入英语，最后成为表示「享受」的通用词。

items.en: Placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to someone, and its noun sense named the state of being agreeable.
items.cn: placere 意为令人愉快、可以接受，其名词用法指「合意」这个状态。

items.en: Old French used plaisir as a noun for enjoyment as well as a verb meaning to please.
items.cn: 古法语中 plaisir 既是名词「享受、快乐」，也是动词「使高兴」。

items.en: The Anglo-Norman form plesir carried the noun into legal and everyday English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，盎格鲁-诺曼语形式 plesir 把这一名词带入英语的法律与日常用语。

items.en: Middle English pleasure covered both the feeling of enjoyment and the favour or consent shown to another person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pleasure 既指享受的感受，也指给予别人的恩惠或同意。

items.en: Modern English keeps the general sense of enjoyment and adds fixed phrases for leisure, willing help and social courtesy.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「享受」这一总义，并固定出表示消遣、乐于相助与社交客套的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjectives and relatives of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for enjoyment.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族里的形容词与同源词；近义组收表示「享受、快乐」的名词。

entries.definition: Enjoyable or nice, especially of a place, taste or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的（多指地方、味道、态度）。

entries.definition: Giving pleasure, often of an experience.
entries.definitionCN: 带来愉快的，多形容体验。

entries.definition: Nice to look at or to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 好看的；令人满意的。

entries.definition: An old word for a pleasant place or a feeling of delight.
entries.definitionCN: 古语，指宜人之地或愉悦之感。

entries.definition: Great pleasure, stronger and more excited than ordinary enjoyment.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的快乐，比一般的享受更兴奋。

entries.definition: A feeling of deep happiness, often shown openly.
entries.definitionCN: 深深的喜悦，常外露。

entries.definition: The pleasure you get from doing or having something.
entries.definitionCN: 从做某事或拥有某物中得到的乐趣。

entries.definition: Satisfaction felt when a desire is met.
entries.definitionCN: 愿望得到满足时的快感。

entries.definition: Something special that gives pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 让人开心的特别享受。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the please family seen from the inside: what started as being agreeable to someone becomes the enjoyment a person carries afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是 please 词族从内侧看的样子：起初是「令某人合意」，后来变成人心里留下的那份享受。

normal.en: Pleasure and please share the Latin base placere, so a pleasure is what being pleased feels like from the inside.
normal.cn: pleasure 与 please 共用拉丁语基座 placere，所以 pleasure 就是「被取悦」从内部感受到的样子。

normal.en: Take pleasure in marks the source: the preposition points at whatever the enjoyment comes from.
normal.cn: take pleasure in 标出的是来源：介词指向让你得到享受的那件事。

normal.en: With pleasure answers a request, turning the enjoyment into willingness to help.
normal.cn: with pleasure 用来回应请求，把这份享受转成愿意帮忙的表态。

normal.en: For pleasure separates an activity from duty, which is why it appears with reading, travel and games.
normal.cn: for pleasure 把活动与职责分开，所以常和读书、旅行、游戏一起出现。

normal.en: The countable plural pleasures names the separate things that each give enjoyment, such as a meal or a visit.
normal.cn: 可数复数 pleasures 指一件件各自带来享受的具体事物，比如一顿饭、一次拜访。

abstract.en: The same root covers being agreeable, being pleased and giving pleasure, because enjoyment is a relation between a person and something else.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根覆盖「合意」「感到满意」「给予快乐」，因为享受本来就是人与某物之间的关系。

abstract.en: A pleasure is never purely inside: it always points back to the thing that caused it.
abstract.cn: 快乐从来不只在心里：它总是指回造成它的那个东西。

abstract.en: When the word becomes a formula of thanks, enjoyment turns into a small social gift.
abstract.cn: 当这个词变成道谢的套话，享受就转成了社交上的一点小礼物。

examples.en: He listened to the rain with quiet pleasure.
examples.cn: 他安静地听着雨声，心里很愉快。

examples.en: Her garden is her greatest pleasure.
examples.cn: 她的花园是她最大的乐事。

examples.en: It was a pleasure to work with such a careful team.
examples.cn: 能和这样细致的团队共事是一件愉快的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来酒」——朋友把好酒扑到你面前，喝下去浑身舒坦，那就是 pleasure。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使愉快）的名词用法经古法语 plaisir、盎格鲁-诺曼语 plesir 进入英语；与 please 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is inward enjoyment; the other senses add the countable source of joy, the leisure use and the courteous formula.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是心里的享受；其余义项分别添上可数的快乐来源、消遣用法与客套说法。

core.cn: 核心意象：身体陷进椅子，一天的紧绷慢慢退去。

branches.cn: 在安静的院子里长舒一口气

branches.en: a garden the owner tends every morning
branches.cn: 主人每天清晨打理的园子

branches.en: a book read on a day off, with no deadline

branches.cn: 主人说这完全不算麻烦

branches.cn: 一家人慢慢吃完的一顿饭

intro.cn: 这个名词保留了表示「令人愉快」的拉丁动词，再靠一个名词后缀和两个英语后缀长出一圈形容词。

definition_en: a stiff piece of paper used for writing, playing games or sending greetings
core_image: 一张硬纸片在手与手之间传递
scene: 新年那天，我给远方的好友寄去一张手写的贺卡。 On New Year's Day I mailed a handwritten card to my faraway friend.
sceneCN: 这里 card 是「贺卡」（第 1 个义项：用来书写或问候的硬纸片）；句意为新年寄出一张手写贺卡。

senses.title: A stiff paper for writing or greeting
senses.definition: a stiff piece of paper with writing or pictures, sent or given to someone
senses.definitionCN: 写有文字或图画、用来赠送的硬纸片
senses.example: She made a card for her teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她给老师做了一张卡片。
senses.why: Greek khartes meant a sheet of papyrus, and the thin stiff sheet kept that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 khartes 指纸草叶，这种薄而硬的纸片沿用了它的名字。

senses.title: Playing cards
senses.definition: small stiff cards with numbers and pictures used in games
senses.definitionCN: 印有数字图案、用来游戏的小硬片
senses.example: They played cards on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在火车上打牌。
senses.why: The same thin sheet became the tool of games, numbered and illustrated.
senses.whyCN: 同一张薄硬片被加上数字图案，成了游戏道具。

senses.title: An identity or bank card
senses.definition: a small plastic card that proves who you are or pays for things
senses.definitionCN: 证明身份或用于支付的小塑料卡
senses.example: He forgot his bank card at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他把银行卡忘在家里了。
senses.why: The small flat object carried identity, just as paper cards carried words.
senses.whyCN: 这片小平片承载身份，正如纸卡承载文字。

intro.en: Card descends from Greek khartes, a sheet of papyrus, through Latin and French.
intro.cn: card 经拉丁语与法语上溯至希腊语 khartes（纸草纸叶）。

items.en: Greek khartes meant a sheet made from papyrus reeds.
items.cn: 希腊语 khartes 指用纸草制成的纸叶。

items.cn: 拉丁语 charta 指纸叶或文件。

items.en: Old French carte named documents and later small stiff sheets.
items.cn: 古法语 carte 先指文件，后指小硬纸片。

items.en: Middle English card meant both paper sheets and playing cards.
items.cn: 中古英语 card 兼指纸片与纸牌。

items.en: Modern English added plastic identity and bank cards.
items.cn: 现代英语又添塑料证卡与银行卡。

note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收纸片与游戏类词。

senses.title: Physical hurt in the body
senses.definition: an unpleasant feeling in the body caused by injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 由受伤或疾病引起的身体上的不适感觉
senses.example: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。
senses.why: Latin poena meant a penalty, so the word starts from something imposed on a person rather than chosen; bodily hurt is felt as a price.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 意为「惩罚」，所以这个词的起点是加在人身上的东西，而不是自己挑的；身体的痛就像被收走的一笔代价。

senses.title: Deep emotional suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of great sadness or distress that is not caused by physical injury
senses.definitionCN: 并非由身体损伤引起、而是源于内心的巨大悲伤或难受
senses.example: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
senses.exampleCN: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。
senses.why: If pain is a penalty paid, it can also be paid in the mind, so the same word covers grief that leaves no visible wound.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pain 是一笔要付的代价，也就可以在心里付；于是同一个词也覆盖了看不见伤口的悲伤。

senses.title: Effort and trouble taken
senses.definition: the effort and careful work that someone puts into doing something properly, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为把事情做好而付出的努力与细心，通常用复数
senses.example: She took great pains to hide the crack in the vase.
senses.exampleCN: 她费了好大功夫才把花瓶上的裂缝藏住。
senses.why: Anything worth doing exactly right costs some discomfort, so the plural pains came to mean the trouble one is willing to spend.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要做到位的事都得付点不舒服的代价，于是复数 pains 转而指人愿意花出去的那份心力。

senses.title: To cause someone hurt or distress
senses.definition: to make someone feel physical or emotional hurt
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到身体上或情绪上的难受
senses.example: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 承认自己错了让他很难受。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by reversing the direction: instead of feeling the penalty, a person or event now imposes it on someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词时方向反了过来：不再是承受那份惩罚，而是某人或某事把它加到别人身上。

intro.en: Pain goes back to a Latin word for penalty, which reached English through French and slowly moved from punishment to the hurt a body or mind feels.
intro.cn: pain 可追到拉丁语中表示「惩罚」的词，经法语进入英语，词义从处罚慢慢移到身体或心里感到的痛。

items.en: Poena meant penalty, punishment, or the price paid for a wrong.
items.cn: poena 意为处罚、惩罚，或为过错付出的代价。

items.en: The adjective poenalis described what belongs to punishment, and it survives in English penal.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 描述与惩罚有关的东西，在英语中留下 penal 一词。

items.en: Old French peine took over the sense of punishment and also of hardship and suffering.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 承接了「惩罚」，也带上「艰苦、受苦」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pain named both the penalty and the bodily hurt, and the bodily sense gradually became the main one.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pain 既指惩罚也指身体的伤痛，后来身体上的痛感渐渐成了主要意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense, adds the emotional one, and keeps the plural as a word for effort.
items.cn: 现代英语保留身体痛感，添上情绪上的痛苦，并让复数形式表示付出的辛劳。

note.en: The look-alike group collects legal relatives of the Latin word for penalty; the near-meaning group collects words for hurt and suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收源自「惩罚」这一拉丁词的司法同族词；近义组收表示伤痛与受苦的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for penalty, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示惩罚的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Relating to punishment by law.
entries.definitionCN: 与法律上的惩罚有关的。

entries.definition: A punishment for breaking a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 因违反规则而受到的处罚。

entries.definition: To long for something sadly; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 苦苦思念；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A continuous dull pain.
entries.definitionCN: 持续而隐约的疼痛。

entries.definition: The state of being tender and painful to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 一碰就疼的状态。

entries.definition: Serious pain of body or mind that lasts.
entries.definitionCN: 持续的身体或精神痛苦。

entries.definition: Extreme worry, sadness or discomfort.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的忧虑、悲伤或不适。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for penalty, and its family runs from legal punishment to bodily hurt and the effort people spend.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「惩罚」的拉丁名词上，同族词从法律处罚一路延伸到身体的痛和人们肯花的力气。

normal.en: Latin poena is a penalty, so pain is something charged to you rather than something you choose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 poena 是惩罚，所以 pain 是被记在你账上的东西，而不是你自己挑的。

normal.en: Penal and penalty keep the legal side of poena visible in modern English.
normal.cn: penal 和 penalty 让 poena 的司法一面在现代英语里仍然看得见。

normal.en: The suffix -ful in painful adds fullness: a thing that is full of pain.
normal.cn: painful 里的后缀 -ful 添上「满」的意思：一件装满疼痛的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -less in painless removes it: a state with no pain at all.
normal.cn: painless 里的后缀 -less 把它去掉：完全没有疼痛的状态。

normal.en: Take pains is the old idea of paying a price, now spent as careful effort.
normal.cn: take pains 原本是「付出代价」的老想法，如今花出去的是细致的用心。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fine now means a hurt, which suggests we treat pain as something the body pays.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经表示罚款的词如今表示疼痛，说明我们把痛当成身体付出的东西。

abstract.en: Pain is the body's way of charging attention to a place that needs care.
abstract.cn: 疼痛是身体把注意力记到某个需要照料的地方。

abstract.en: The plural pains reminds us that careful work also has a cost, just a quieter one.
abstract.cn: 复数 pains 提醒人：细心的活儿也有代价，只是安静一些。

examples.en: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
examples.cn: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。

examples.en: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
examples.cn: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。

examples.en: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
examples.cn: 承认自己错了让他很难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩恩」——佩恩磕到桌角，疼得直吸凉气；pain 就是疼痛。

root: 拉丁语 poena（惩罚、代价）经古法语 peine 进入英语；一般认为词义由「受罚」转到「受苦、疼痛」，同族词多与处罚、痛感有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hurt that costs you something; the senses divide into bodily pain, grief of the mind, the effort one pays out, and the act of hurting someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一种要你付出代价的痛；义项分为身体的痛、心里的苦、肯付出去的辛劳，以及让别人难受的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed to the ribs while a sharp ache narrows the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住肋侧，一阵刺痛让眉头皱起。

branches.en: a hand pressed hard against a sore knee
branches.cn: 一只手紧紧按住发疼的膝盖

branches.en: an empty chair that still hurts to look at
branches.cn: 一把看一眼就难受的空椅子

branches.en: a careful hand hiding a crack in a vase
branches.cn: 一只手小心地把花瓶裂缝遮住

branches.en: a face that has just heard its own mistake named
branches.cn: 刚听到自己错误被点破的一张脸

branches.en: one word holding a wound and a grief together
branches.cn: 同一个词同时装着伤口和悲伤

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin noun of penalty, its adjective, and two English suffixes that add or remove pain.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示惩罚的拉丁名词、它的形容词，以及两个给「痛」添上或去掉的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Poena, the Latin noun for penalty, and its adjective poenalis stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 poena（惩罚）及其形容词 poenalis 是英语这个词背后的来源。

由 pain 加 -less 构成，指无痛的

definition_en: a raised floor for performing, a period in a process, or to present a play or event
core_image: 灯光亮起，演员走上舞台中央
scene: 演员走上舞台。 The actor walked onto the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 stage 是「舞台」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演员走上舞台。

derivatives.zh: 上演；临时搭建
做作的；戏剧化的
舞台艺术

senses.title: Performing platform
senses.definition: a raised floor where actors or musicians perform
senses.definitionCN: 演员或乐手表演用的抬高平台
senses.example: The actor walked onto the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上舞台。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的具体义项。

senses.title: Period of a process
senses.definition: a particular point or period in a process
senses.definitionCN: 过程中的某个时刻或时期
senses.example: The project is at an early stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目正处于早期阶段。
senses.why: The platform became a step in time.
senses.whyCN: 「台」的概念延伸为时间上的「台阶」。

senses.title: Put on a show
senses.definition: to arrange and perform a play, concert, or event
senses.definitionCN: 安排并演出戏剧、音乐会或活动
senses.example: They staged a new play last night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们昨晚上演了一出新戏。
senses.why: The verb returns to the theatre sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词义又回到戏剧场景。

intro.en: Stage comes from Latin stare, to stand, through Old French estage, a dwelling or floor.
intro.cn: stage 经古法语 estage（住所、楼层）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Estage meant a dwelling or a floor.
items.cn: estage 意为住所或楼层。

items.en: Stage named a raised floor or platform.
items.cn: stage 指抬高的地面或平台。

items.en: The theatre sense became dominant.
items.cn: 戏剧舞台义后来占据主导。

items.en: The time sense grew from step by step.
items.cn: 时间义由「一级一级的台阶」引申而来。

note.en: Stage is compared with look-alike words and words for periods.

normalIntro.cn: stage 是抬高的台、时间中的一步，也是把戏搬上台的动作。

normal.en: He has stage fright.

normal.en: They staged a concert.

abstract.en: The world watches what you stage.

branches.en: Curtains open and the play begins.
